Alibaba Cloud Releases Qwen4-Max with 25% Lower Singapore API Prices

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alibaba Cloud released Qwen4-Max through Model Studio on November 16, 2026, introducing a flagship multimodal model with a one-million-token context window and lower list prices than Qwen3.8-Max.
  • The Singapore price list sets Qwen4-Max at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, compared with $2 and $6 respectively for Qwen3.8-Max.
  • It has been revealed that the model documentation describes text, image and video input with text output, alongside streaming, web search, parallel tool calling, function calling, prefix completion and structured JSON output.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alibaba Cloud released Qwen4-Max through Model Studio on November 16, 2026, introducing a flagship multimodal model with a one-million-token context window and lower list prices than Qwen3.8-Max.

The Singapore price list sets Qwen4-Max at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, compared with $2 and $6 respectively for Qwen3.8-Max. Both rates are 25% lower, calculated directly from those list prices. A one-million-token free quota is also available in Singapore for 90 days from the latest of Model Studio activation, model release or application approval.

It has been revealed that the model documentation describes text, image and video input with text output, alongside streaming, web search, parallel tool calling, function calling, prefix completion and structured JSON output. Developers can call the model through OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages or Alibaba Cloud’s DashScope APIs, providing several established integration routes for coding and agent software.

Alibaba Cloud designed Qwen4-Max for coding, office productivity, frontend design and complex agentic tasks. Thinking is enabled by default at high reasoning effort, with low, high and xhigh settings available. Its 131,072-token default thinking budget matches the maximum non-thinking output, while thinking and the final answer share a 262,144-token allowance, so deliberation occupies part of the same output budget as the response.

According to recent reports, the Qwen4 caching guide says identical input prefixes, such as system prompts, tool descriptions and reference documents, can be reused across requests from the same user. An explicit cache’s prefix must contain at least 1,024 tokens, with five-minute or one-hour lifetimes available. Explicit breakpoints provide deterministic hits for an identical prefix within the validity period; ordinary implicit caching identifies common prefixes automatically but does not guarantee hits. Automatic caching can also place a breakpoint at the end of the input, allowing it to advance as a conversation grows.

According to recent reports, in Singapore, cache reads cost $0.075 per million tokens for either caching approach, while explicit-cache creation costs $1.875 for a five-minute cache and $3 for a one-hour cache. Only input tokens receive the cache discount; output tokens remain at the standard price. For agents that repeatedly send long instructions or documents, prefix stability and cache lifetime therefore influence whether lower input charges accompany the reduced list rates.

Industry observers note that qwen4-Max is listed in Beijing, Singapore, Frankfurt, Virginia, Tokyo and Hong Kong. Batch inference is supported only in Beijing among those locations, while fine-tuning and custom model deployment are unsupported throughout the documented regions. API configuration, reasoning settings and caching therefore carry much of the practical control over how the managed model is used.

In a recent development, the full Qwen4-Max is also included in Singapore’s Personal Edition Token Proposal, which bills through Credits and supports interactive tools including Claude Code, Cursor, Qwen Code, Qoder and OpenClaw. The subscription is limited to interactive coding and agent-tool use; automation scripts, custom application backends and non-interactive batch calls are prohibited. That makes the plan a distinct access route from ordinary pay-as-you-go API calls.

The full release follows Qwen4-Max-Preview, which became available at 10:00 on November 11, 2026 (UTC+8) exclusively through Token Plan. Its preview is scheduled to run through November 25, 2026, after which the preview model will be retired.

Recent findings suggest that qwen4-Max’s lower list rates and caching options address input costs for long-running agent workloads, but the final bill still depends on output length, reasoning and cache reuse. With fine-tuning and custom deployment unsupported, those usage controls and the choice between API and subscription access are central to the release’s practical impact.

#591. Alpine Linux People Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (832 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Infoq

Alpine Linux People Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Infoq

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • InfoQ Homepage News Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw.
  • Nov 16, 2026 4 min read.
  • The flaw comes from the way OpenSSH checks passwords when musl handles the underlying crypt() call.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

InfoQ Homepage News Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw.

Nov 16, 2026 4 min read.

The flaw comes from the way OpenSSH checks passwords when musl handles the underlying crypt() call. On an affected system, a password longer than 256 bytes causes musl to return an error value. That value is an asterisk, the same character Linux uses in /etc/shadow to mark an account as having no password. OpenSSH then treats the returned asterisk as a match and permits the login.

The conditions to exploit the vulnerability are however quite narrow. The server must run OpenSSH before version 10.6p2, be built against the musl library rather than glibc, and operate without PAM. It must also have at least one account with a SHA-256 or SHA-512 password hash and another account marked with an asterisk in its shadow entry. When those conditions are met, any password between 257 and 1,024 characters can authenticate against the passwordless account.

Industry observers note that alpine Linux is the most prominent distribution affected, as it uses musl and its default OpenSSH configuration does not enable PAM. Other musl-based environments, including OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto, may also be affected where the same configuration applies. Systems using glibc, PAM, Dropbear or OpenBSD are not affected.

Sources indicate that ozgun Kultekin, a security researcher at Wakefield, published the technical explanation on the *sshole site. Kultekin traces the problem to two musl changes made in 2012: the first replaced the NULL error return from crypt() with an asterisk, and the second added a 256-byte limit to SHA-512 password hashing, so longer inputs caused an error. Together, the changes produced a value that could be mistaken for a password hash.

It has been revealed that the OpenSSH side of the problem dates from a 2016 fix for CVE-2016-6210, which was a timing attack that could reveal whether a username existed. To make responses take a similar amount of time for valid and invalid users, OpenSSH borrowed the salt from another account and hashed the supplied password anyway. That workaround also applied to real accounts whose shadow entry contained an asterisk.

Kultekin writes that the issue remained unnoticed for roughly a decade because the vulnerable combination was uncommon in testing. OpenSSH is tested on OpenBSD and glibc-based systems, while many Linux distributions route authentication through PAM, which does not call crypt() for asterisk entries in the same way. Kultekin says the bug was found after building OpenSSH in several configurations and testing about 17,600 unusual login attempts.

Sources indicate that on Alpine's official AWS and Azure images, the default alpine user is marked as passwordless and can use doas without a password. This means that an attacker who reaches that account can therefore obtain root privileges. Dan Goodin reports for Ars Technica that the matter can give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts within seconds on affected systems.

In a recent development, openSSH 10.6p2 contains a fix. Operators who cannot update immediately can disable password authentication by setting PasswordAuthentication no in the SSH server configuration and restarting sshd. Kultekin also advises checking authentication logs for evidence that an account with no password accepted a password. The project has published a detection and background repository.

Recent findings suggest that the vulnerability is being actively exploited. Goodin notes that GreyNoise reported that honeypots in Southeast Asia had been attacked by a group it is tracking known as GT10, which reportedly deploys a backdoor which supports shell commands, reconnaissance and persistence. Goodin reports that watchTowr linked the activity to botnets and cryptocurrency operations, while Previdian recorded 20 exploitation attempts from 13 IP addresses in nine countries. The United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added CVE-2026-123158 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 9 November, according to Hackread.

Red Hat has stated that its products are not affected because they do not meet the required combination of musl and no PAM. Amazon has likewise marked Amazon Linux 2 and Amazon Linux 2023 as not affected. That does not remove the risk for teams running Alpine-based containers, embedded devices or custom musl builds. Administrators should look for SSH servers built against musl, check whether PAM is disabled, review shadow entries for asterisk-locked accounts, apply OpenSSH 10.6p2 and restart the service.

The vulnerability was publicly disclosed on 5 November and exploitation reports followed within days. For organisations with internet-facing SSH services, the immediate action to take is fairly straightforward: revision OpenSSH, restart it, and remove password authentication where it is not needed.

SambaNova Pairs Intel GPUs with SN50 for Air-Cooled AI Inference

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SambaNova Systems declared on November 15, 2026 that it and Intel had demonstrated an air-cooled AI inference system at SuperComputing 2026, running GLM-5.3 across four Intel GPU D-Series accelerators for prompt processing and a SambaRack SN50 for token generation.
  • The system divides inference into prefill, which processes an incoming prompt and builds its key-value (KV) cache, and decode, which generates output tokens.
  • According to recent reports, the demonstration is much smaller than Intel’s reference configuration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SambaNova Systems declared on November 15, 2026 that it and Intel had demonstrated an air-cooled AI inference system at SuperComputing 2026, running GLM-5.3 across four Intel GPU D-Series accelerators for prompt processing and a SambaRack SN50 for token generation.

The system divides inference into prefill, which processes an incoming prompt and builds its key-value (KV) cache, and decode, which generates output tokens. Intel’s hardware handles compute-heavy prefill, while SambaNova’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Units (RDUs) handle memory-bound decode. SambaNova presents the recorded system as a design customers will be able to deploy in existing brownfield data centers.

According to recent reports, the demonstration is much smaller than Intel’s reference configuration. SambaNova describes an 80-GPU D-Series reference rack delivering 208 petaflops of peak FP4 compute, with 12 TB to 38 TB of memory depending on configuration. Those figures specify the larger prefill design; they are not performance measurements from the SuperComputing setup.

Industry observers note that intel’s D270 product specifications list a 350 W air-cooled GPU with 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX matrix engines, standard PCIe 5.0 and up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory per card. The standard form factor is intended to work in existing servers without proprietary networking or bespoke systems.

Each SambaRack SN50 contains 16 RDUs and typically requires 20 kW for inference. As many as 16 racks can operate as one unit with up to 256 RDUs, spreading a workload across lower-power racks. SambaNova says its dataflow architecture chains model operations across chips instead of returning data to memory between separate GPU kernels, reducing memory traffic and kernel-relaunch overhead during token generation.

NVIDIA Dynamo sits in front of the two accelerator pools and is designed to route each request toward the hardware already holding its cached context. vLLM serves both the Intel prefill path and SN50 decode path, while NIXL transfers KV-cache data over UCX/RDMA using standard RoCEv2 Ethernet. The handoff can therefore use an established Ethernet fabric rather than a proprietary interconnect between the hardware types.

Industry observers note that SN50 retains KV prefixes from earlier prompts in attached DDR memory, while on-chip SRAM and HBM support active decoding. When an agent returns to a conversation or shared context, cache-aware routing can send the request to the SN50 holding that prefix, so only latest material goes through GPU prefill and less KV state crosses the network. SambaNova notes these cache hits shorten time to first token and free GPU capacity for new requests. The post describes those benefits without reporting measured latency or throughput results for the combined demonstration.

The split also lets providers expand each phase independently. Longer prompts can call for more D-Series prefill capacity, while agents producing longer outputs can require additional SN50 decode capacity, without proportionally expanding the other pool.

According to recent reports, that flexibility is aimed at operators whose facilities cannot easily accommodate liquid-cooled systems. Intel says the D270’s standard PCIe form factor and 350 W air-cooled profile are designed for existing racks without a specialized liquid-cooling retrofit. Combined with SN50’s rack-level power profile, the design is intended to add inference capacity within established air-cooled environments.

The demonstration’s significance is the integration: two accelerator architectures, connected by commonly used serving software and standard Ethernet, can be assigned to different inference phases and scaled according to workload. For providers facing fixed power and cooling limits, the remaining question is whether production workloads realize enough of the described caching and utilization benefits to justify operating both pools.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The American Psychological Association released Deploying AI into Workplaces: What Leaders Need to Know on November 16, 2026, setting seven objectives for organizations introducing artificial intelligence into employees’ work.
  • The guide is for organizations that have chosen to adopt AI; it does not answer whether they should.
  • Sources indicate that the guidance addresses a gap in workplace policy awareness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The American Psychological Association released Deploying AI into Workplaces: What Leaders Need to Know on November 16, 2026, setting seven objectives for organizations introducing artificial intelligence into employees’ work. The guide addresses trust, human oversight, job design and worker well-being.

The guide is for organizations that have chosen to adopt AI; it does not answer whether they should. Its checklist supports introducing, using and evaluating tools, with examples of effective implementation and red flags to watch for. The stated aim is responsible adoption that supports employees and improves how work is designed.

Sources indicate that the guidance addresses a gap in workplace policy awareness. In APA’s 2026 Work in America survey, fewer than 40% of workers for whom the question applied reported knowing whether their employer had an official policy on acceptable AI use. The Harris Poll conducted the online US survey for APA among 2,009 employed adults from May 21 to June 1, 2026.

Sources indicate that the survey also found that 48% of workers worried AI could make some or all of their job duties obsolete, the highest level since the question was introduced in 2023. Meanwhile, 37% worried they would fall behind colleagues if they did not use AI, up from 30% in 2025, while 64% believed technological change was benefiting employers more than workers, compared with 52% in 2025.

Industry observers note that “Purchasing an AI tool and telling people to use it without further direction is not a sound strategy,” said Dennis P. Stolle, APA’s executive lead psychologist for applied psychology. He said employers should give workers information about where tools are reliable and where they are not, ensure meaningful human oversight and rethink job designs.

Job design receives its own objective because tasks and the broader role may both need redesign. Its considerations include mental workload, attention, awareness of the wider work situation, hidden labor and incentives. The guide identifies the amount and distribution of verification work in AI-assisted roles as an emerging evidence question, putting verification duties inside the deployment discussion.

Recent findings suggest that the expertise objective seeks to preserve opportunities to develop deep knowledge, share it and learn from experience. It highlights skill decay, deskilling and the performance problems that can arise when people are out of the loop, making skill formation part of AI deployment rather than a separate training issue.

It has been revealed that other objectives address how workers judge and control systems. Employers should help people develop and adjust their trust over time, make human oversight meaningful rather than a formality, and clarify where responsibility sits in mixed human-AI work. Safeguards should match the stakes of potential errors, with consequences and future scenarios considered.

Fair process requires consultation with people who will use a system and those affected by its outputs. Voice, transparency, consistency and the ability to correct outcomes are among the relevant principles. The final objective calls for psychological boundaries and limits on monitoring, covering privacy, autonomy, dignity and surveillance. It also treats the validity of AI-enabled inferences about workers’ internal states as an emerging evidence question.

Sources indicate that APA recommends using the checklist before a significant deployment and periodically afterward, discussing it with people who understand both the technology and the affected work. The objectives should be revisited on a regular schedule and after a latest system, a model change, a major upgrade or a reorganization. Organizations should record vital decisions, their owners and when they will be reviewed; which objectives matter most depends on the work, goals and risks.

Industry observers note that the document is not a compliance standard, an APA professional standard or an evaluation of any product. Its evidence framework distinguishes decades of research on topics such as trust in machines, error detection, attention, job performance and organizational change from newer findings about current AI systems. APA treats those emerging findings as provisional, not settled. The advisory panel that informed the guide spanned human-technology interaction and clinical, social, legal, cognitive and industrial-organizational psychology.

For employers, the practical implication is that AI deployment becomes a continuing test of work design. The assessment extends beyond the tool to whether workers can judge its reliability, exercise real oversight, build expertise and participate in decisions as both the system and their jobs change.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Daisytuner confirmed on November 16, 2026 that it had raised €6 million in seed funding and released Daisyflow, an AI inference engine that serves models inside customers’ own infrastructure and adapts their execution to different hardware.

Elaia and LEA Ventures co-led the round, with participation from Amadeus APEX Technology Fund and Seedcamp. Daisytuner said the capital will be used to bring Daisyflow to more enterprises, grow its team and expand its compiler technology.

In a recent development, daisytuner reports that its first results show Qwen 2.5 running up to 18% faster than vLLM on AMD Instinct GPUs. The result gives the launch a specific performance data point as the company presents Daisyflow for a broader range of model categories and accelerator suppliers.

In a recent development, at the center of the technology is docc, Daisytuner’s open-source compiler. It translates PyTorch, NumPy and C/C++ into a dataflow intermediate representation, a format that makes data movement, parallelism and computation explicit, then generates native code for NVIDIA’s CUDA and AMD’s ROCm platforms and for novel architectures. This addresses the manual performance work that can arise when a latest model or chip disrupts existing optimizations.

AI agents search for optimizations and benchmark them on real hardware. docc verifies each optimization for correctness before use, and proven recipes enter a performance database. During later compilation, the compiler can match those recipes to similar code, allowing knowledge from earlier workloads to inform new optimization work.

The hosted Daisytuner Platform turns this into a developer workflow with continuous benchmarking on GitHub pushes, a browser-based optimization editor and the performance database. Users can inspect hotspots measured on real hardware, create optimization recipes and submit the results as pull requests. Daisyflow builds on that optimization layer by adding production model serving.

Recent findings suggest that the docc repository publishes the compiler under the new BSD license. Its compatibility matrix lists Linux support for C/C++, Python and PyTorch frontends with OpenMP, CUDA and ROCm backends. The PyTorch frontend supports inference only rather than training.

In a recent development, daisyflow serves language, vision, speech and recommendation models. Its inference layer routes requests to models, batches and schedules work for hardware utilization, and coordinates multi-step and agent workflows. Applications connect through standard APIs, with OpenAI compatibility for language models, and a ready-to-use chat interface is included.

In a recent development, the Daisyflow product page lists deployment on premises, in a customer’s data center or in a private cloud, with NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Tenstorrent as accelerator options. Requests, data and outputs remain within the customer’s infrastructure. Daisytuner assesses workloads, hardware and costs, installs the system, ports models to the selected accelerators and remains involved in operation and tuning.

Daisytuner is targeting cloud providers with mixed hardware fleets, enterprises that want control over data and execution, and hardware vendors seeking faster production integration. The deployment model connects those audiences: customers choose or own the infrastructure, while Daisytuner supplies the optimization and serving layers and works with them on operations.

It has been revealed that the funding supports both sides of that offer: wider enterprise deployment and a compiler system intended to reduce manual integration as fresh models and chips arrive. The central challenge is breadth, extending the early AMD performance result across the model types, accelerator vendors and customer environments Daisyflow is designed to support.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Associated Press reported on November 16, 2026, that governance specialists see Anthropic’s planned initial public offering as a test of whether its mission can withstand pressure to deliver profits, with the company’s public-benefit structure leaving wide latitude to decide how social benefit is measured.

In a recent development, anthropic’s amended IPO registration statement, filed on November 10, 2026, defines its specific public-benefit purpose as the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. Delaware law requires its directors to balance that purpose with stockholders’ financial interests and the interests of people materially affected by the firm’s conduct.

According to recent reports, sarah Kreps, director of Cornell University’s Tech Policy Institute, stated “the real test emerges if and when the question of public benefit becomes costly,” or when it conflicts with making a profit. That distinction matters because the legal structure requires directors to balance competing interests without prescribing which must prevail in a particular business decision.

The Long-Term Benefit Trust is designed around five financially disinterested voting trustees with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy and social enterprise. A single Class T share lets the trustees vote as a unit and generally elect and remove the Class T directors who constitute a majority of the authorized board. The share carries no economic rights.

That authority over board seats does not extend to running Anthropic. The filing expressly says neither the trust nor its trustees has decision-making authority over day-to-day management or strategy. Their role is to select directors equipped to balance the organization’s three obligations and to support management through advice and guidance.

According to recent reports, the founders hold a separate source of control. A single Class F share to be issued to the seven co-founders’ Founder LLC immediately before completion of the offering will carry 50.1% of general voting power, including elections of non-Class T directors, and will have no economic rights. The arrangement divides influence between trustees who can shape most board seats and founders who retain majority voting power on matters submitted to stockholders generally.

Sources indicate that UC Berkeley law professor Stavros Gadinis stated the trust’s accountability power is consequently limited: trustees who disagree with directors could face a difficult removal process and might be unable to remove a majority. Three directors are elected directly by the trust and three by other shareholders. A seventh cannot be appointed or removed without consent from the board’s nominating committee, which is expected to be controlled by the founders.

Anthropic contributed Class N shares representing 5% of its fully diluted shares as of June 30, 2026, under the filing’s stated conversion assumption, to its wholly owned Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. The board may matter additional shares representing up to 2% of outstanding shares plus specified convertible and fund-held securities each time the share price rises 50% above the prior milestone. Separately, the co-founders have pledged 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to philanthropic causes.

Anthropic’s October 18, 2026 announcement noted it established the fund as an LLC rather than a 501(c)(3) to retain flexibility among forms of giving. None of the fund’s Anthropic equity will be used for lobbying or political giving.

Those commitments define potential resources for public benefit more clearly than they define the result. Kreps said public benefit is likely harder to measure than profit and that competition, including from open-source Chinese models, could pressure AI developers to reconsider guardrails. The measurement question therefore sits alongside the control question: even a well-resourced mission needs a way to judge whether it is being met.

Gadinis said public-tech giant financial reporting, outside questions and companies’ interest in investor trust could provide an additional accountability mechanism. Required disclosure and scrutiny from investors may generate more information about Anthropic’s decisions than was available while it was private.

Recent findings suggest that the practical test is whether the trust, founders and board use their respective powers when safety and financial interests diverge, and whether public reporting gives outsiders enough evidence to assess those choices. Anthropic’s governance and public-reporting obligations create channels for accountability, but the meaning and measurement of humanity’s long-term benefit remain open to judgment.

Industry News: Uno Platform 7.0 Adds WebGPU Backend, Apple TV and Reactor Support, and Retires Native Rendering

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • InfoQ Homepage News Uno Platform 7.0 Adds WebGPU Backend, Apple TV and Reactor Support, and Retires Native Rendering.
  • Nov 16, 2026 3 min read.
  • The Uno Platform team released Uno Platform 7.0, which unifies rendering on SkiaSharp 4 with an experimental WebGPU backend, adds Apple TV as a target platform and supports .NET 11 from day zero.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

InfoQ Homepage News Uno Platform 7.0 Adds WebGPU Backend, Apple TV and Reactor Support, and Retires Native Rendering.

Nov 16, 2026 3 min read.

The Uno Platform team released Uno Platform 7.0, which unifies rendering on SkiaSharp 4 with an experimental WebGPU backend, adds Apple TV as a target platform and supports .NET 11 from day zero. The release also brings third-party .NET MAUI controls and Microsoft.UI.Reactor library to every target, and removes native rendering and Mac Catalyst.

Uno Platform is an open-source framework for building .NET applications with C# and WinUI XAML for Windows, Android, iOS, macOS, Linux and WebAssembly. The team describes 7.0 as its largest release, with 5,219 commits and 704 closed challenges since 6.7. According to the team’s benchmarks, 7.0 is about 2x faster at the median and 5x smaller than 6.7, with some operations, such as brush creation, up to 38x faster. These figures come from the vendor and the workloads were not published in detail.

All targets now render through one pluggable pipeline. SkiaSharp 4 is the default, and Uno Platform is a co-maintainer of the library alongside the .NET team at Microsoft. On Android, Windows and Linux, Skia now renders through Vulkan by default. The WebGPU backend, available on all desktop, mobile and WebAssembly targets, is enabled by adding WebGpu to UnoFeatures and registering the backend on the host builder. It uses wgpu-native outside the browser and the browser’s own WebGPU support on WebAssembly. The team measured up to a 50% frame-rate improvement depending on the scene, and indicates a WebGPU-only app drops about 6 MB of uncompressed native code from WebAssembly builds. A new WebGpuCanvasElement lets applications concern their own WebGPU commands inside the UI.

Through .NET MAUI Embedding, controls from vendors such as Syncfusion, Telerik, Infragistics, DevExpress and Esri previously ran only on iOS, Android, macOS and Windows. They now work on every Uno Platform target, including the web and Linux. In the other direction, existing .NET MAUI apps can reach the browser and Linux through Uno Platform’s .NET MAUI handlers.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft.UI.Reactor, Microsoft’s declarative C# framework for WinUI with hooks such as UseState and no XAML, now runs on desktop, browser, Android and iOS. It is enabled with the Reactor UnoFeature, is in preview, and can coexist with existing XAML pages in the same visual tree. Apple TV support is added through the net10.0-tvos target framework, targets tvOS 15 and later, renders through Metal and uses the Siri Remote for focus navigation. .NET 11 is supported on every head, for example through dotnet new unoapp -tfm net11.0, while .NET 10 remains the long-term support option.

RichTextBlock and RichEditBox are now available on every platform, closing an matter opened in 2018. WinUI alignment continues with ItemsRepeater and ItemsView ported from current WinUI sources, LinedFlowLayout, the TitleBar control, multiple windows on iPad and Lottie rendering through Composition. Smaller additions include built-in input validation through INotifyDataErrorInfo, TalkBack, VoiceOver and AT-SPI screen-reader support, and the uno-devserver app command for launching and inspecting running apps from scripts and CI.

It has been revealed that most apps upgrade by changing the Uno.Sdk version in global.json, following the migration guide. The team released Uno Platform Studio 3.3 alongside it.

Recent findings suggest that the release follows Uno Platform 6.7 in September, which added Android TV, Android Auto and Wear OS targets, semantic styles shared by the Material and Simple themes, and damage-region repainting on Skia renderers. It also removed the WPF targets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mercari declared on November 16, 2026 that it had decided to form Mercari Surugaya Inc. with Suruga-ya, a US venture for Japanese entertainment and hobby products. Mercari will own 51% of the Delaware manufacturer, which is planning AI-supported appraisal, pricing, inventory and product-discovery operations.

According to recent reports, the venture is planned for December 2026, with Shunsuke Sako as representative and Suruga-ya holding the remaining 49%. Its activities will cover online sales and purchases, procurement and physical-store operation. US activity is planned to start in Los Angeles, with products also sold through Mercari US and the Mercari Global App. Service launch dates remain undetermined.

Appraisal, product registration and price setting are among the retail processes the companies want to make more efficient with AI. The planned applications also cover purchasing, product catalogs and inventory management. Shoppers would see separate applications in item search and supplementary product information. The announcement provides no performance results for these planned uses.

According to recent reports, mercari CEO Shintaro Yamada said the venture would evolve “operations with AI at the core,” connecting that approach to Mercari’s ambition to build a global marketplace. Suruga-ya CEO Tsunashige Sugiyama described the entity as a major step toward his company’s long-held goal of expanding seriously in the US.

Industry observers note that the retail operation also has a data purpose. Mercari states US market-price and demand data can only be obtained through actual transactions in that market. Suruga-ya’s catalog and appraisal knowledge will supply product context for records generated by those transactions. The combined information is intended to improve the user experience in search, recommendations and authenticity verification, while also supporting both parent companies’ businesses.

Mercari is contributing US distribution and its experience with consumer-service design and AI. Suruga-ya’s contribution is built around specialist inventory, procurement, appraisal and sales expertise. The release puts its retail network at 160 stores in Japan and overseas as of October 2026, with tens of millions of items in inventory and catalog data covering more than approximately 30 million products. Its specialties include figurines, trading cards, games and anime merchandise.

In a recent development, the two companies already had a capital and business partnership, concluded in December 2025. The earlier agreement covered inventory coordination and combined online and offline distribution, as well as aims to connect Suruga-ya’s catalog and authentication knowledge with Mercari’s transaction data and AI technology. Since then, Suruga-ya items have been sold through Mercari.

According to recent reports, the planned entity would give that collaboration a jointly owned US operating base, with local procurement and store operations alongside Mercari’s sales channels. It also places AI inside the design of the retail business, with transactions intended to generate data for subsequent services. The central execution question is whether the companies can build that data loop from Los Angeles and combine Suruga-ya’s specialist knowledge with Mercari’s technology to deliver efficient retail work and more useful product information for US buyers.

A step down to the Galaxy A57, which I found to be one of my favourite mid-range smartphones of the year, the Galaxy A37 is a great no-frills Samsung handset with some respectable specs — a 6.7-inch 120Hz Super AMOLED display, three rear camera lenses, a 5,000mAh battery with 45W fast charging, to name a few. In a recent development, while Black Friday is technically on November 27, deals often start much earlier from retailers, telcos and brands across Australia. In a recent development, but if you're in the market for a latest iPhone, we won’t expect as many deals, as Apple’s handsets don't usually see the same major price drops as Android rivals. Without question, the best kind of display you can get is AMOLED, as it offers deep blacks and individually-lit pixels, allowing for always-on-displays that consume very little battery due to the majority of the screen turned off. Various types of OLED displays are featured in most top models, including the Samsung Galaxy S26, iPhone 17, Google Pixel 10 ranges and more. Sources indicate that there are a huge number of Android handsets on offer from several major manufacturers, which all generally have their own strengths (and occasional weaknesses). It has been revealed that when looking at a phone's camera array, you should consider the types of photos that you want to take. If you want to photograph wildlife or other things you can't easily get close to, then a telephoto lens is essential, with zoom a key factor to consider, while for landscapes a good ultra-wide is your friend.

But of course, still photography isn't the be all, end all. If your needs are more centred around video recording, you will want to track assets like the resolution at which a camera phone shoots video, stabilisation features (for action video) and capture modes.

When you have at least a general idea of what you need from your phone's camera, you can get a better picture of which phone camera setup is for you, with our best camera phones list helping you to easily find which options tick the right boxes for what you might need.

Depending on how much you're willing to spend, Android phones offer varying degrees of performance, with top handsets like Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra and Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max offering plenty of grunt under the hood thanks to their top-of-the-line specs.

You’ll find that, among the Snapdragon, Exynos and MediaTek chip families, the more powerful the processor, the higher the model number.

Apple's iPhones, on the other hand, often pack a similar amount of horsepower depending on which generation of device they belong to. Both guarantee terrific performance and will continue to do so for a couple more years yet. After that, you may start to notice some slowdown, depending on how power-hungry Apple makes its next iOS iterations.

Industry observers note that most manufacturers will offer their handsets with various amounts of onboard storage. Depending on what you want to do with your phone, you'll want to settle on a storage size that's right for you. Smartphone storage can range anywhere from 64GB to 2TB (realistically, you'll be seeing between 128GB and 1TB in most cases), though you can expect the price to rise significantly as that number gets larger. Some Android phones will offer expandable storage via a microSD card slot, meaning you can add more capacity should you ever need it.

There are plenty of savings to be had in the final month before the Australian financial year comes to a close, and that makes it a great time to save a packet on the latest phones.

As is always the case, more recent models like those from Apple's iPhone 18 Pro range and the Samsung Galaxy Z foldable lineup won't be seeing the biggest discounts (although we suspect something in the 10-20% range may arrive, and more likely with the latter), but models from the previous generation or more mid-range handsets are quite likely to get hefty savings applied to them.

This means that we may see savings on the more affordable iPhone 17e and models like the iPhone 17 and Samsung Galaxy S26 ranges will be had for a bargain as retailers want to clear their stock.

For example, Vodafone and Optus discounted the iPhone Air and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra by up to AU$800, as long as you got them on either a 12-, 24- or 36-month plan. You can expect more of these this year, although the better discounts and wider variety of handsets will likely be on outright purchases.

According to recent reports, flagship Pioneering announced on November 16, 2026 that it is establishing Flagship Origination Lab, U.K. in London, backed by an initial £100 million commitment. The lab will conceive, test, fund and build AI-native platform companies, and is Flagship’s first dedicated manufacturer-creation unit outside the United States.

Industry observers note that operating within Flagship Labs, the London unit will focus on human and planetary health and other frontiers of science and technology. It brings a firm-creation model developed in Cambridge, Massachusetts, into a locally rooted UK ecosystem connected to Flagship’s global organization.

Founder and CEO Noubar Afeyan mentioned Flagship anticipates scaling its commitment through partnerships to attract an additional £500 million. The additional amount depends on future partnerships and remains separate from the capital committed at launch.

Flagship expects to recruit and train approximately 50 scientist-entrepreneurs and operators for the initial UK team. The local tech giant-creation ecosystem will remain connected to the broader organization, including its Pioneering Intelligence and Pioneering Medicines business units.

Sources indicate that flagship’s model starts with scientific questions and develops them into platforms, products and companies. The firm says it has created more than 130 companies over more than 25 years, including Moderna, providing the tech giant-creation record it is now extending to the UK.

Avak Kahvejian, president of Flagship Labs and a general partner at Flagship Pioneering, described origination as a discipline led by teams of scientist-entrepreneurs who “begin with bold questions about what could be possible.” The London team will accordingly be involved in generating and testing ideas as well as financing and building the resulting companies.

Industry observers note that that structure gives Flagship a role from the earliest stage of company formation. Rather than operating solely as an investor in existing startups, the lab is designed to originate the underlying scientific platforms and then build businesses around them within its own ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the launch follows three years of Flagship partnering and conducting R&D across the UK. It opened a London office and signed a memorandum of understanding with the UK government in 2023 to extend the global reach and impact of its companies.

Flagship describes Quotient Therapeutics, released during that period, as its first transatlantic company. Its UK activity also includes clinical trials involving Flagship-founded companies such as Generate:Biomedicines, alongside partnerships across academia, data and regulatory innovation.

It has been revealed that kahvejian said the UK’s science base, clinical-trial infrastructure, genomics and health-data assets, agile regulatory environment, and scientists and entrepreneurs made it a deliberate choice for the expansion. Those resources provide the foundation on which Flagship intends to build its local company-creation operation.

Chris McDonald MP, Minister for Science, Innovation and Investment, remarked the government wants more AI and life-sciences businesses to turn research and technology into jobs and economic growth, with Flagship’s commitment helping new UK companies take breakthroughs to international markets.

The expansion adds local firm origination to Flagship’s existing UK research, partnerships and clinical activity. Its larger financial ambition depends on attracting partners, while the lab’s operational test is whether the newly introduced team can turn those scientific and clinical assets into new AI-native companies.

This wand also dispenses fresh hot water for Americanos or non-coffee drinks. There is a frother whisk tucked into the side of the machine that just froths your milk, which is perfect for cold foam (or hot foam if you pre-heat your milk).

In a recent development, as with any coffee machine, you'll need to clean everything after you're done brewing. Many of the parts can go into the dishwasher, and the parts that do need to be hand-washed are quick and easy to clean.

In a recent development, I brewed many different styles of coffee beverages. It's hard to imagine a type of drink that you couldn't make quite easily with the De’Longhi All-In-One Combination Coffee & Espresso Machine.

I started by making a single eight-ounce cup of coffee. I pulled out the platform and set my mug upon it. According to recent reports, the night before I wanted a pot of coffee, I set up the Auto-On function and measured out the appropriate amount of coffee for a half carafe. I woke up about an hour after my coffee was ready and found it still fresh and quite hot. You can adjust the time and temperature of the warming plate, but I just used the default.

In a recent development, I brewed a single espresso with ease. I chose the smaller filter basket and inserted it into the portafilter. The user guide recommends running a warm-up cycle with just water so I did that first. Then I used the included measuring scoop and put the grounds into the filter basket. I made an espresso as directed. As the user guide suggested, I started with 3.5 ounces of milk in a container that can hold a lot more than that. I used a full-fat oat milk. The froth had big bubbles which were quite sturdy and held up well to stirring. This was quite tasty.

In a recent development, A latte is similar to a cappuccino, only instead of added steamed milk plus lots of froth, you just add steamed milk. At least, that's a latte according to the user guide. In general coffee terms, a cold brew is brewed in the refrigerator for eight or more hours for a strong but smooth brew. Brewing was slow, it took about 12 minutes to brew eight ounces of lukewarm coffee. This wasn't my favorite setting to be honest. Once I added ice, the coffee went pretty weak.

This special setting brews a small amount of coffee very strongly, intended to be brewed over ice. I measured the recommended amount of coffee into the reusable coffee filter. I put a container half-filled with ice on the coffee platform, as the user guide suggested. I used the eight-ounce Over Ice setting and it took only three minutes to brew. This is a quarter of the time it took to brew the same size serving of cold brew. I preferred this method for making iced coffee, it tasted better to my palette. The coffee strength held up better to the ice using this setting.

The frother whisk is different from the steam wand. It foams but doesn't add any steam to your milk. It also doesn't change the temperature. I decided to make an iced coffee with cold foam using some of the iced coffee I had made previously. I put a few ounces of oat milk into a small glass jar and frothed it. It swiftly tripled or quadrupled in volume, though for some reason it wasn't as airy-looking as my steamed foam was. I poured what I wanted into my mug. The foam held up well to stirring.

  • Nov 16, 2026 4 min read.
  • It has been revealed that AWS has rolled out Nitro Sandboxes, which run an opted-in Kubernetes pod, ECS task, or EC2 workload inside its own lightweight virtual machine with a separate guest kernel, carved out of a running EC2 instance by the Nitro hypervisor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

InfoQ Homepage News AWS Nitro Sandboxes Put Each EKS Pod in Its Own MicroVM with One RuntimeClass Field.

Nov 16, 2026 4 min read.

It has been revealed that AWS has rolled out Nitro Sandboxes, which run an opted-in Kubernetes pod, ECS task, or EC2 workload inside its own lightweight virtual machine with a separate guest kernel, carved out of a running EC2 instance by the Nitro hypervisor. On Amazon EKS, the whole change is one pod field: runtimeClassName: isolated-sandbox or confidential-sandbox.

It has been revealed that the feature is available in all commercial regions at no additional charge, and AWS positions it for workloads where the tenant or the code cannot be trusted, with coding agents named first. In an AWS blog post, Carlos Santana and Trishi Mehta write:.

Each pod gets its own operating system, completely separate from the host and from every neighbor.

Recent findings suggest that according to the EKS documentation, a containerd-shim-nitro-sandbox-v2 process on the parent instance launches a Firecracker microVM as a first-level guest with hardware-assisted virtualization, after which an agent inside the VM runs the pod’s containers through its own containerd and the two sides communicate over virtio and vsock. The result is a sandbox that shares neither kernel nor memory mappings with the parent instance or any other sandbox, while the containers themselves start unchanged. How the nodes get there depends on the cluster type: on EKS Auto Mode the two RuntimeClasses ship with every cluster and sandbox-capable nodes are provisioned on demand, whereas on standard EKS a team builds a sandbox-enabled AMI for its node groups or Karpenter.

(Source: Amazon EKS User Guide).

What separates the two modes is which side of the boundary is trusted. Isolated mode trusts the parent instance and not the guest, which is why kubectl exec, logs, and process listing keep working, whereas confidential mode treats the parent as untrusted and moves enforcement inside the VM: a Cedar policy generated from the pod spec pins image digests, arguments, environment, mounts and capabilities, exec and stdin are denied, the Nitro Secure Module measures the image and policy into PCRs, and a KMS key policy can release secrets only to a sandbox whose measurements match. Image layers can be encrypted as well, so the parent moves ciphertext it never reads.

That chain only holds if something checks the measurements, and the documentation indicates so: without a KMS policy or external verifier checking the PCR values, "the attestation measurement is recorded but never verified, and the confidentiality guarantees of confidential mode are incomplete." Separately from either mode, a network-isolated annotation boots the sandbox with no network device at all, which also removes DNS, NTP, IMDS and Pod Identity and breaks HTTP and TCP probes.

According to recent reports, sandip Das, an AWS Container Hero, read the documentation the same way and drew out what isolated mode leaves to the operator: the protection "only runs in one direction," so a compromised parent can still observe or tamper with unencrypted traffic and DNS, writes the pod's /etc/hosts, and can mint Pod Identity credentials for any pod on the node. He also lists prerequisites the blog post does not, among them Kubernetes 1.36 or later, a launch template with Nitro Enclaves enabled on managed node groups, without which "sandboxed pods sit in Pending," and Pod Identity rather than IRSA for credentials. On AWS's description of performance as near-native, he advises treating it "as a vendor claim" and benchmarking startup latency, I/O throughput and tail latency.

Beyond agents, AWS lists multi-tenant SaaS, regulated workloads, CI builds and remote IDEs, and points to the open-source agent-sandbox project for warm pools that hand out a pre-booted VM in about two seconds.

Sources indicate that the constraints are on the considerations page, and the largest is GPU and device passthrough, which is not supported at launch because Firecracker cannot pass host devices into a guest, so GPU pods run without the sandbox class. Density is capped twice over: total sandbox vCPUs may not exceed five times the node's vCPU count, and neither may the number of sandboxes, halved on CPU-overcommit types, which gives a 4-vCPU node room for twenty 1-vCPU sandboxes or five 4-vCPU ones. Simultaneous multithreading costs more than the arithmetic suggests, because core scheduling stops two sandboxes sharing the sibling threads of one core and leaves roughly half the advertised vCPUs usable; Graviton, with one thread per core, is unaffected.

Industry observers note that the nearest comparison is GKE Sandbox, which has offered a gvisor RuntimeClass since 2019 and more recently a microvm class built on Kata Containers and Cloud Hypervisor. gVisor intercepts syscalls in a user-space kernel, starts in under 200 milliseconds and supports CUDA on a subset of GPUs; Google's microVM option carries a fixed 250 mCPU and 130 MiB per pod, starts in one to two seconds and does not support GPUs. AWS has taken the VM side of that split and expressed its overhead as density and threads rather than per-pod resources.

Industry observers note that on EC2, Amazon Linux and Firecracker are supported natively and patches are available for other virtual machine monitors. The EC2 User Guide carries the supported instance list and notes that snapshot, restore and live migration are not available.

Breaking: Developer creates a 100% valid ZIP file that doubles as a BIOS-bootable operating system

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hacking stories these days mostly involve someone using an army of AI agents to find vulnerabilities in networks and software that were carefully hidden in plain sight.
  • You can unpack the ZIP file just like any other, boot it using Linux's GRUB, QEMU, or any other Multiboot-compatible loader (even if imaged to different media), or alternatively, perform the finest party trick: image-write it to a floppy and boot from it directly from BIOS on any compatible PC, without modification.
  • It has been revealed that much like me, that sequence of words may be triggering a head-tilt reminiscent of a confused puppy, so we'll explain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hacking stories these days mostly involve someone using an army of AI agents to find vulnerabilities in networks and software that were carefully hidden in plain sight. Today, for a change, we have a story about hacking in its original meaning — twisting computing artifacts into purposes not in their design spec. David Oberhollenzer, aka Goliath, a greybeard in spirit if not in shade, crafted a 100% valid ZIP file that's simultaneously an archive, BIOS-bootable, and a Multiboot-compatible OS image.

You can unpack the ZIP file just like any other, boot it using Linux's GRUB, QEMU, or any other Multiboot-compatible loader (even if imaged to different media), or alternatively, perform the finest party trick: image-write it to a floppy and boot from it directly from BIOS on any compatible PC, without modification.

It has been revealed that much like me, that sequence of words may be triggering a head-tilt reminiscent of a confused puppy, so we'll explain. The first thing you need to know is that unlike most file types, the metadata (in this case, file directory) of a ZIP is actually at the end of the archive. Up to that point, the data is comprised of every compressed file in sequence.

The file packs all have a predictable structure: "PK" followed by bytes 03 04, metadata (including name), some extra/comment fields, and then the file's contents. Notably, any file can be stored uncompressed, and Goliath made use of that for the very first file, called ZIPHEAD.COM — remember, this is the start of the ZIP archive.

Sources indicate that goliath mentioned that it was "easy" to make the ZIP file a valid Multiboot system image. A valid image only needs to contain bytes 0x1BADB002 in the first 8 KiB, followed by some flags and a checksum. It was trivial to place that datum in ZIPHEAD's data, along with the location of where the bootloader lies.

Grub or QEMU don't care about anything else in the image, as once they have the initialization information, from that point it's the bootloader's problem. The actual bootloader, predictably, is in ZIPHEAD's uncompressed data, and the image will happily boot directly, or, say, from a floppy.

According to recent reports, making the same exact archive bootable via a standard PC BIOS took a little more work and some clever shenanigans. Making a disk bootable is simple enough: the BIOS reads the first exact 512 bytes of the disk's contents, and if they end with bytes 0x55AA, then it's bootable, and the BIOS starts executing whatever code is the first byte.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Placing 0x55AA precisely at position 510 of the ZIP, already in ZIPHEAD's contents, is once again simple, and won't corrupt the Multiboot image, as if you'll recall, the Multiboot spec is flexible with data locations. But you may wonder: once the BIOS runs code in sequence starting from the ZIP's first byte, then ZIPHEAD's header ("PK" + 0x0304, plus all metadata) surely is garbage for practical purposes, and not proper code? Well, yes, but actually no.

The first four bytes represent CPU instructions that don't write anything to memory, so they're harmless, other than a push-to-stack. The next few belong to ZIPHEAD's metadata, and Goliath massaged those values to represent instructions that would either be innocuous or perform operations he could use, namely using the modification time bytes as instructions to jump further down the data.

Sources indicate that sounds simple, but the actual process of choosing bytes that represent (1) non-crashy CPU instructions, (2) useful code for setting up the boot process, and (3) still represent a valid file header in a ZIP archive is far trickier than the above. Do go and check out the full blog post if you want all the details.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, moth announced Tessa on November 16, 2026, reporting that the method encoded and recovered 1,568 real values across all 120 qubits of IBM’s Phoenix Nighthawk r2 processor.
  • Sources indicate that daniel Bultrini’s paper gives the claimed record a specific scope: experiments that loaded freely chosen numeric lists onto physical quantum processors and retrieved the individual values, excluding runs that returned only a derived quantity.
  • In a recent development, tessa, short for Tessellated QPIXL, alternates data and address qubits in a checkerboard laid over the processor’s physical connections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, moth announced Tessa on November 16, 2026, reporting that the method encoded and recovered 1,568 real values across all 120 qubits of IBM’s Phoenix Nighthawk r2 processor. The work addresses a persistent obstacle for quantum machine learning: loading classical data into fragile qubits on sparsely connected hardware.

Sources indicate that daniel Bultrini’s paper gives the claimed record a specific scope: experiments that loaded freely chosen numeric lists onto physical quantum processors and retrieved the individual values, excluding runs that returned only a derived quantity. Under that definition, QCrank previously recovered 128 values from 12 trapped-ion qubits. A separate Fez experiment recovered 1,024 pixels from 13 qubits, but is not directly comparable because it used a trained tensor-network approximation rather than an arbitrary list of real values. The paper therefore identifies Tessa’s run as the largest reported under its definition.

In a recent development, tessa, short for Tessellated QPIXL, alternates data and address qubits in a checkerboard laid over the processor’s physical connections. Each data qubit is controlled only by neighbouring address qubits, which nearby data qubits can share. Every additional address neighbour doubles a data qubit’s storage, so an interior qubit with four neighbours holds 16 values.

The construction works on any bipartite coupling graph, where every coupler joins a data qubit to an address qubit. Using the device’s own layout avoids SWAP gates and routing, and requires no ancilla, or helper, qubits. The paper proves that values on each data qubit remain independently recoverable despite the shared controls.

All values stored in a single basis can be decoded from one round of computational-basis measurements across the chip. Tessa can also store a second number in each slot’s phase. The Phoenix run used this pair mode for an image’s brightness value and hue, placing two numbers in each of 784 used slots; spare slots held zeros so every qubit participated.

That density has two costs. Pair mode adds measurement bases and doubles circuit depth. More generally, shots are divided among local address configurations, so the number needed for equivalent accuracy grows exponentially with local coupling degree, although the experiments kept that degree small.

In a recent development, single-basis tests used 8,192 shots per basis to recover a 28-by-28 QCAT image using 784 of Phoenix’s 792 slots and a 21-by-21 image using 441 of Fez’s 448 slots. The paper reports raw hardware value correlations of 0.96 on Phoenix and 0.95 on Fez, with mean absolute errors of 0.130 and 0.131, respectively. Dynamic-range recovery, which uses summary statistics of the input rather than the input itself, reduced those errors to 0.075 and 0.078. The experiments used no error mitigation.

It has been revealed that the 1,568-value pair run was less accurate: the paper reports a value correlation of 0.69, value mean absolute error of 0.152 and hue mean absolute error of 0.092 on Phoenix. Its circuit used 1,456 two-qubit CZ gates, compared with 728 for the single-basis Phoenix run. Full-chip retrieval therefore worked on two coupling graphs, but the second phase value came with higher circuit demands and lower reconstruction quality.

Beyond pixel art, the experiments covered audio, MIDI, DNA and protein amino-acid sequences, including p53. The biological sequences were chosen for their lengths or names, not their biology, making these tests of data handling rather than biological analyses.

At 32,768 shots per measurement, the paper reports that Phoenix recovered the 784-nucleotide MT-CO3 sequence with 92.1% of nucleotides exactly correct without post-processing and 92.3% with the best tested dynamic-range recovery, selected using the true sequence. Recovery remained worse for densely packed protein sequences. The paper cautions that even one incorrect nucleotide or amino acid can have serious biological consequences.

Industry observers note that moth indicates Tessa is available for image-processing experiments on its Atlas platform. The repository’s documentation provides the library, raw hardware counts, job records, simulation outputs and notebooks that regenerate the paper’s figures and tables without an IBM account. Its run log dates the principal Phoenix and Fez QCAT experiments to September 26, 2026, and later genetic and pixel-art runs to October 2026, distinguishing the hardware work from the November announcement.

Tessa’s immediate contribution is a hardware-aware way to load and verify classical data across an entire processor. For quantum machine learning, the central open question is whether subsequent computations can exploit that encoded state without paying for full reconstruction, while keeping shot growth and the errors of denser pair encoding under control.

  • The main flash controller is the Silicon Motion SM2320G, one we have reviewed in portable SSDs like the Kingston XS2000 and Lexar SL660 Blaze, with a separate C*Core CCM4101 microcontroller — which has 2MB of flash and a small amount of RAM to itself — for the 428 x 142 color LCD.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, doom now runs on a USB flash drive’s built-in LCD and is played by copying files to and from it, as hardware hacker Aaron Christophel highlighted in a teardown video. The marking on the drive’s display chip had been removed, but an open debug port let him extract its firmware, which enabled identification. He was then able to use AI to reverse-engineer the hardware and get the game running on the drive’s screen.

The off-the-shelf drive, the MOVESPEED MSSU10, has USB-A on one end and USB-C on the other, and the 128GB model, the smallest capacity in the range, cost him about 50 euros. Its screen normally shows status data such as transfer speed, how full the drive is, and its temperature.

The main flash controller is the Silicon Motion SM2320G, one we have reviewed in portable SSDs like the Kingston XS2000 and Lexar SL660 Blaze, with a separate C*Core CCM4101 microcontroller — which has 2MB of flash and a small amount of RAM to itself — for the 428 x 142 color LCD. The NAND carries SanDisk markings. All of this is fairly standard portable SSD hardware, aside from the display.

It has been revealed that the drive’s metal body uses heavily glued plastic end pieces but, past that, the display lifts off first and unplugs. The board slides out after the USB-C end cap is removed, in this case with minor cosmetic damage inflicted. The display chip’s marking is scrubbed, most likely with a laser, by the hacker’s reckoning, which can hinder identification and tinkering. Luckily, a probe on the debug pads, ground, and a 3.3V pin connected on the first try, and memory was immediately readable.

According to recent reports, the bootloader returned a version string dated 2023, followed by the full firmware, which helped greatly with identification. He states the chip is marketed as one for security — for fingerprint readers and access control, for example — but no related features were found to be enabled for this drive. He also discovered that, although the data sheet and stock firmware declare a 200 MHz operating clock frequency, it measured 40.2 MHz. This is unexplained.

One critical issue is immediately apparent: how do you play on a drive with no buttons? The display chip has no USB connection of its own and, from the connected PC or host, it only sees the storage controller’s activity, which it uses to gauge transfer speed. The primary storage controller has read and write counters, and the chip pulls these every 50 ms over I2C. Christophel states this is far easier than relying on a single physical button, as he did on a previous power bank mod.

The solution, then, is a PC script, doomctl.py, which turns key presses into small, timed transfers in each direction. The commands are simply encoded as transfer rates, at five levels per direction, and each read/write pair can map to a certain button combination. Arrow keys are for movement and turning, Space or Ctrl for firing and opening doors, and M for the menu, keeping it simple. Ordinary copying, without the script, can still steer, but the control scheme is much nicer.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Industry observers note that performance is…well, not really playable at about 13 frames per second, although the game logic runs at Doom’s normal 35 ticks per second. This is why he names the chip’s clock as the biggest potential performance gain. The game itself is built on DMC100-DOOM, Artur Bieniek’s port for very small microcontrollers. Only the first map, E1M1, fits in the chip’s flash, and no sound is produced as the drive lacks a buzzer. Christophel did play the level end to end, noting the low resolution.

AI did the heavy lifting: the reverse engineering as well as the port, and Christophel remarked, “I would not be able to do such a thing in a few hours.”.

The open-source project, with its code and prebuilt firmware published, is likely to draw attention and may spawn similar hacks. The tools required are relatively minimal, mainly a debug probe, and he does suggest backing up the stock firmware before trying. For his own unit, he put it back together to use as a normal drive, but one that can still play Doom, if so desired.

Post-training uses self-distillation from Hy4, with reinforcement learning cutting average end-to-end output tokens by 50%.

For serving, Tencent indicates megakernels, four-bit quantization and DFly push decoding speed beyond 150 tokens per second, enabling lower-cost deployment at scale.

Rather than emphasize public benchmark scores, Tencent built WorkIndex around typical WorkBuddy tasks, measuring deliverable quality, single-turn output length and task turnaround time. Its eight evaluation sets cover slide creation and editing, human-AI slide co-writing, human-AI Markdown co-writing, document editing, spreadsheet repair, audio/video processing and visual understanding.

Tencent reports that Hy4 flash performs slightly above Hy4 preview overall on WorkIndex, while average cost per task falls to one-thirteenth of Hy4 preview, one-twentieth of Hy4 and one-eighth of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at Max-tier peak-hour pricing.

A separate blind evaluation involved 85 internal WorkBuddy owners working through 259 tasks across 27 categories. Tencent reports user satisfaction close to Claude Haiku 5.5, along with the shortest end-to-end completion time and the lowest cost per task among the evaluated models.

Industry observers note that hy4 flash is available through Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, Yuanbao, WeCom, QQ, ima and Marvis, with OpenRouter availability planned. WorkBuddy access is free through November 30, 2026, while TokenHub API usage receives a 50% discount until 12:00 Beijing time that day. The discount covers only usage generated during the promotional period.

For developers, the API identifier is hy4-flash. Tencent Cloud’s model documentation lists image understanding, reasoning, structured output, function calling and caching, with maximum input and output limits of 960,000 and 64,000 tokens, respectively. Its API overview adds support for OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages, and requires customers to activate the model service before making calls.

It has been revealed that tencent recommends Hy4 flash for deep search, document processing, slide creation, simple frontend demonstrations and computer use, while continuing to recommend full Hy4 for complex, long-horizon software engineering because of its higher intelligence ceiling. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you were affected by last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage, chances are you had trouble accessing your email. You probably didn’t expect to be poisoned as a result, yet that’s exactly what happened to over a dozen unfortunate hotel guests in Germany — but Microsoft has reported that the blackout wasn’t caused by a cyberattack.

According to a news report from German outlet WDR (via Notebookcheck), 15 guests at a hotel for the Phantasialand theme park were injured when the park’s swimming pool received excessive levels of chlorine. This was caused by a malfunction in the chlorine monitoring system, but because alerts are sent to park staff over email — and because those email systems were down due to the Microsoft 365 outage — no one knew about the problem until guests started getting sick.

According to a Facebook post made by the fire department that responded to the incident, 40 first responders were dispatched and 15 guests were triaged after the chlorine gas leak. WDR reported that the affected people suffered from respiratory irritation, with four needing to be taken to hospital.

Industry observers note that the episode illustrates the serious — and often unexpected — consequences that can arise when something as central to a business’s operations as an email system goes down. When it’s responsible for crucial safety procedures, the results can be potentially life-threatening.

In a recent development, since the outage, Microsoft has mentioned that full service has been resumed. It has since published a post-incident report, which is available in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center portal. The full write up has also been relayed on Reddit.

In the report, Microsoft revealed that the outage was caused by three principal factors: a “latent defect” from July that overwhelmed Windows servers; a Microsoft Teams failure that increased the load on a system shared with Microsoft Exchange; and the fact that 14% of server capacity for the networking system was out of service at the time.

Taken individually, these factors were not enough to cause the global failure. But when the increased load and the lower server capacity combined, they triggered the latent defect. Server requests then piled up until the servers stopped responding — which happened to occur during the peak traffic window for the United States.

As a mitigation effort, traffic was automatically redirected towards healthy endpoints. However, this process made those endpoints more likely to themselves encounter the latent defect. “This caused a cascading failure from server to server as the same amount of load was spread across fewer servers,” Microsoft wrote. At its worst point, the outage had caused 80% of available servers to become unresponsive.

Due to a separate concern, Microsoft’s bulwarks against such a cascading failure did not function properly. Recovery took longer than expected because restored servers were immediately overwhelmed by pent up traffic, making them fail once again. And because the latent defect dated back to July, simply rolling back to a recent version was not enough.

According to recent reports, to fix the outage once and for all, Microsoft had to return its code path to that of a previously good state, then take servers offline in batches, roll out the patch across its infrastructure, then restart its systems. Eventually, service was restored.

Industry observers note that the post-incident report is a sobering reminder of what can happen when several seemingly independent problems can converge all at once, and of the consequences that are possible when that happens on such a large scale. And as the chlorine incident in Germany demonstrates, these failures often go beyond mere technical disruption and touch on people’s health and wellbeing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ROBOTERA declared the commercial launch of its XHAND 1 Pro-U on November 16, 2026, opening orders for an initial 40-unit release of the five-finger dexterous robot hand, according to its launch release.

Sources indicate that the launch follows the 16-degree-of-freedom hand’s use in NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 research, including a DexUMI demonstration presented by Jim Fan at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL). ROBOTERA is targeting research teams, robotics developers and industry partners working on dexterous manipulation, robot learning and real-world robotic applications.

According to recent reports, ROBOTERA designed the Pro-U around NVIDIA GEAR Lab’s DexUMI exoskeleton, a wearable device that records human demonstrations without requiring a robot. The firm notes corresponding joints map movements directly between the exoskeleton and robot hand, reducing additional motion conversion. The redesign also adjusts thumb positioning, palm-side tactile sensing and articulation for natural demonstrations and varied grasping postures.

The GR00T 2 whitepaper notes GEAR DexUMI reproduces the XHAND1 Pro-U’s joint kinematics, contact surfaces, wrist-camera mount and tactile-data format, with a one-to-one mapping onto the robot’s joints. Each GEAR DexUMI unit combines 15 magnetic encoders for finger-joint tracking, an OAK wrist camera and fingertip sensors for normal and shear force. Two units can be worn together to record bimanual demonstrations.

During collection, a wearer manipulates real objects directly while DexUMI records hand movements, wrist-camera video and fingertip forces. Those demonstrations are used to post-train GR00T 2, and the learned skills run on a dual-arm Tianji robot fitted with two XHAND1 Pro-U hands. For the three evaluated tasks, post-training used only the wearable demonstrations, without task-specific teleoperation or additional general robot-motion data; no operator remotely controlled the target robot during collection.

The force recordings also shape control. NVIDIA converts fingertip forces into joint torques and adds them to the robot’s action targets. During execution, predicted torque lowers each joint’s stiffness and offsets its position target, allowing the hand to apply the predicted force while accommodating positional uncertainty. That mechanism supports contact-rich actions such as slicing, unscrewing a lid and striking a match.

NVIDIA publishes the DexUMI hardware designs and documentation under CC BY 4.0, excluding vendor product photos, and its data-collection software under Apache-2.0 by default. The vendor’s XHAND robot-description files are separately MIT-licensed, while ROBOTERA’s commercial hand supplies the execution side of the same workflow.

The evaluation covered three multi-step sequences combining tool use, hand-to-hand transfers and lid handling. Banana-yogurt preparation involved drawing a knife, slicing the banana, removing the yogurt lid and moving pieces into a bowl. Granola scooping required passing a jar between hands, unscrewing its lid and using a spatula. In fire chemistry, the robot struck a match, lit a lamp beneath a flask and extinguished the match in water.

In NVIDIA’s evaluation, GR00T 2 achieved overall success rates of 60% for banana yogurt, 80% for granola scooping and 75% for fire chemistry. GR00T 1.7 and π0.5, post-trained on the same DexUMI demonstrations with the same data recipe, completed none of the three full tasks. These are results for the specified test sequences, not a general reliability figure for other tasks or operating environments.

Pairing openly licensed capture designs with a commercial matching hand gives research teams a specific route to collect force-aware demonstrations without tying up the target robot. The remaining constraint is execution: the results demonstrate transfer across all three sequences, but the unsuccessful trials leave consistent end-to-end performance as the open question for broader deployment.
