📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scale AI revealed Scale for Hospital Operations on November 16, 2026, launching five AI applications for scheduling, order guidance, medical-record review, safety investigations, and clinical documentation, with availability to health systems beginning the same day.

In a recent development, each application can run on any model inside the health system’s own environment, and deployments include Scale engineers and clinical subject-matter experts. Scale describes clinician evaluation, local data retention, and development alongside customers as its requirements for hospital AI.

Scale also mentioned it spent the year before the launch working inside hospitals, including a U.S. health system it described as top-ranked but did not name, on work aimed at helping clinicians identify safety events sooner. The five applications form the first part of a broader portfolio, with additional applications and agents planned for the months after launch.

The Scheduling Intelligence Agent is designed to triage referrals by clinical urgency and match visits to slots based on room and equipment requirements and physician preferences. It can rearrange existing schedules for urgent patients and coordinate visits across specialties. The Order Guidance Agent reviews patient history, flags missing tests, and recommends laboratory work, imaging, and prescriptions with cited evidence for clinician review.

Industry observers note that for information-heavy work, the Medical Record Review & Summarization Agent assembles a patient history from scattered records and links each extracted finding to its source for checking. The Safety & Incident Investigation Agent prioritizes safety events and searches for recurring patterns, so teams can investigate higher-risk incidents first instead of processing reports only in arrival order. The Clinical Documentation & Quality Review Agent drafts reports for clinician review and sign-off, checks documentation against hospital guidelines, and requires auditors to confirm each finding.

The announcement connects the portfolio to three Scale Labs healthcare benchmarks. CliniCARE-Bench uses real, de-identified longitudinal electronic health records, with 25 clinician-validated scenarios instantiated across 750 cases spanning 14 specialties and ten reasoning skills. It separates cases lacking data from those that remain medically ambiguous, logs retrieval and citations, and scores evidence grounding, policy grounding, process adherence, and calibrated abstention, meaning appropriate deferral when a record cannot support a definitive answer.

Scale Labs reports that the 16 agentic systems it tested achieved raw accuracy of 65.3% to 76.1%, but defect-free accuracy fell by 4.8 to 14.8 percentage points when prohibited reasoning shortcuts were penalized. Every system under-abstained, committing to definitive answers more often than deferring on cases the record could not settle. Those are benchmark findings for the tested systems, not reported validation results for the five hospital applications.

Recent findings suggest that two related benchmarks extend that approach. PSEBench contains 5,074 patient-safety triage cases built around Minnesota’s 29 Reportable Adverse Health Events, including complete, missing-information, and uncertain variants, and was used to evaluate 15 language models. DistressBench contains 718 clinician-authored conversations across 23 suicide and self-harm subcategories. Scale Labs reports that in 35.3% of conversations where a model fully recognized a crisis, it still did not direct the user toward human help.

Scale states this research underpins custom evaluations built around each health system’s workflows while also providing a common way to compare models. That emphasis on ambiguity and process connects with the review controls described for order guidance, record checking, report sign-off, and audit findings.

A 2025 JAMA Network Open study cited by Scale examined 263 ambulatory clinicians across six U.S. health systems using the same Abridge ambient AI scribe for 30 days; it did not evaluate Scale’s products. In its adjusted analysis, estimated burnout prevalence decreased from 51.9% to 38.8%. Participants also reported improvements in note-related cognitive load, after-hours documentation, and focused attention on patients.

The results support the administrative-burden rationale for AI documentation tools, but they concern outpatient use of a different product rather than the fresh hospital-operations portfolio. The researchers listed important qualifications: participation was voluntary, surveys were not anonymous, outcomes were self-reported, and there was no control group to account for temporal trends. Those constraints limit what the 30-day before-and-after results establish, particularly as Scale extends the administrative-burden argument from outpatient documentation to scheduling, orders, and safety triage.

Recent findings suggest that for health systems, the launch’s central question is whether evaluations built around their own workflows can verify evidence retrieval, policy compliance, and appropriate deferral alongside answer accuracy. Scale’s benchmarks show how correct answers can conceal flawed processes; the new applications’ source links, cited recommendations, clinician sign-off, and auditor confirmation are the mechanisms intended to expose those problems to human review.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The CEO of Proofpoint has urged companies of all sizes to be on guard against new and advanced cyber threats built and enabled by the rise of AI.
  • Speaking at the manufacturer’s recent Proofpoint Protect Tour London 2026 event, Sumit Dhawan warned that customers should, “think of AI agents as insiders in your environment” as the number of AI-assisted attacks continues to rise.
  • The organization recently released research claiming AI enables cybercriminals to operate at a scale 'never seen before' - so how does it suggest companies stay safe?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The CEO of Proofpoint has urged companies of all sizes to be on guard against new and advanced cyber threats built and enabled by the rise of AI.

Speaking at the manufacturer’s recent Proofpoint Protect Tour London 2026 event, Sumit Dhawan warned that customers should, “think of AI agents as insiders in your environment” as the number of AI-assisted attacks continues to rise.

The organization recently released research claiming AI enables cybercriminals to operate at a scale 'never seen before' - so how does it suggest companies stay safe?

In his keynote, Dhawan declared that “the concept of time in cybersecurity keeps shrinking”, giving the example of a recent cyber heist which took place in just 27 seconds.

“An agentic toolkit is now able to identify vulnerabilities, matter attacks, and create multiple social engineering campaigns in an automated fashion,” he added, “in this world, we believe that making sure that your human perimeter is protected, because reachability becomes one of the biggest things - and the defence needs to be done with proper understanding of intent.”.

Dhawan outlined Proofpoint’s strategy of Defend with Intent, and Access with Intent, the former looking to understand where attacks originate and how to build resiliency and defense, especially with AI giving attackers a whole new arsenal of tools.

The latter looks to ensure humans and AI can continue to work effectively together, as agents don’t access data or apps the same way humans do, necessitating a whole upcoming approach to make sure company systems are safe.

In a later media Q&A session, Dhawan and Daniel Blackford, head of threat research at Proofpoint, expanded on the role that AI is playing in these newly introduced threats, noting how quickly the threat landscape has changed.

“I think things have changed,” Blackford claims, “threat actors have gone on a similar AI journey that a lot of us have,” although he notes that there is still an adoption and learning curve, as attackers and defenders alike try to discover the best way to utilize AI.

“The problem I see is not whether it's hype or not - but what you do about it,” Dhawan adds, noting how the need for constant and rapid reaction to threats is promptly going to become fatiguing for workers - so the crucial consideration is what businesses do about it.

“It's somewhat of a thankless job, you're always chasing a major threat,” he notes, “ (but) every organization has to invest in getting the right configuration of access and data.”.

“Defenders have had a window where we've been ahead of where threat actors were with using AI - but that window is shrinking,” adds Blackford.

This may be particularly key for small businesses - and I ask Dhawan and Blackford what advice they have for SMBs looking to stay ahead of the latest threats.

“For small businesses, in the past, cybersecurity for them was a little bit of basic hygiene - do I have my antivirus, my firewall, some kind of email spam filtering that also catches some of these threats - now, it’s a real glitch,” Dhawan indicates, pointing to Proofpoint’s recent acquisition of Hornetsecurity as its bid to offer thorough protection for SMBs.

“It’s quite important for small and medium businesses to take (cybersecurity) more seriously now than they ever have,” Blackford adds, noting that these firms could suffer immensely from a lack of reputation due to suffering an attack.

Ultimately, Proofpoint sees its mission as attempting to protect its customers from the biggest number of threats it can - with its recent acquisition of Varonis demonstrating its intent to offer AI-related protection like never before.

“Protection is not meaningful if it doesn't work with everything you have in your environment,” Dhawan noted, pointing out that as the average business can now see millions of AI prompts and actions in a typical year - a mammoth task which simply cannot be manually audited and investigated by humans alone.

“We're doing our part of protecting the behavior, and ensuring your data is connected when people and AI work in this agentic workspace,” Dhawan declared in his speech, “our goal will always be that we integrate (and) by having focus, we are able to do what we do best.”.

“This is the power of AI and the community working together to defeat threat actors.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that garage doors are subject to a number of common problems, and a number of them concern the springs. Because they're tasked with counterbalancing the weight of the door itself, which can be tremendously heavy, a garage door's springs endure a lot of tension and occasionally need to be fully replaced. Don't worry: replacing a spring is considerably less expensive than replacing an entire garage door system.

It has been revealed that typically, replacing a spring will cost between $150 and $350 based on nationwide averages, most commonly landing close to $250. Prices will vary based on the type of spring. Torsion springs, which are the ones mounted above the opening of the metal shaft, are slightly more expensive, at around $75 to $150, while extension springs, the horizontal springs along the side tracks, are cheaper, around $50 to $100 per.

Recent findings suggest that the remainder of the cost is labor, which will also vary by installer and by the number of springs you need replaced, but you can expect to pay between $75 and $150. While the cost isn't insignificant, replacing garage door springs is one of several home improvement projects you really should leave to the professionals.

There are some methods for extending the life of your springs, like spraying them down with the best lubricant for garage doors, which coats them in a thin film that will help protect them. When the time does come to replace them, however, the installer will likely advise replacing both matching springs at the same time.

Paired springs that were installed at the same time will have endured the same number of lift cycles and roughly the same amount of wear cross their lifespan. This means that the partner of a failed spring will also be pretty likely to fail around the same time; knock out both at once and you can save yourself making a second call soon after. It may also save you on things like service fees that get charged per visit regardless of labor.

According to recent reports, as to why you should let a pro handle your spring replacement, it's primarily a safety problem. A typical garage door can weigh upwards of several hundred pounds, and that weight puts the springs under incredible mechanical tension. Without the specialized tools in a professional installer's kit, messing with those springs can lead to sudden, violent release, which can cause severe injury or property damage. A certified pro has the training and equipment to safely uncoil or adjust a spring without risking harm, or damage to your garage or vehicle.

Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (648 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Infoq

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • InfoQ Homepage News Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data.
  • Nov 16, 2026 2 min read.
  • Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

InfoQ Homepage News Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data.

Nov 16, 2026 2 min read.

Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models (LLMs) to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before sufficient real search traffic is available.

Natural language search allows guests to describe their preferences in everyday language, such as "romantic cabin near skiing" or "pet-friendly beach house that sleeps eight", rather than relying exclusively on predefined filters. Training such systems presents two challenges: generating queries that reflect actual user behavior and determining which property listings are relevant to each query.

Previous approaches, including InPars and Promptagator, address query generation and relevance labeling as separate tasks. They use LLMs to generate queries from documents or examples, followed by additional model-based judgments to assign relevance labels. According to the researchers, this separation can introduce additional sources of error and differences between synthetic and real-user query distributions.

Recent findings suggest that CASTLE uses contrastive listing pairs derived from de-identified booking sessions. When a guest books a property after viewing several alternatives, the selected listing becomes a positive example, while another viewed but unbooked property serves as a negative example. An LLM is then prompted to generate a query that matches the positive listing but not the negative one. This allows relevance labels to be established through the construction process rather than through a separate evaluation step.

It has been revealed that the framework combines three query-generation strategies: template-based prompts, few-shot prompts using approximately 500 seed queries collected through targeted user research, and attribute-grounded prompts focusing on distinguishing listing characteristics. A variety mechanism also encourages variation in query length and phrasing.

It has been revealed that for listing pairs without sufficient booking history, including newly listed properties, CASTLE uses a Virtual Judge, an LLM-based evaluator that assigns relevance labels to additional query-listing pairs. The researchers also developed CASTLE-R, a variant intended for production environments where real search traffic has started to accumulate.

According to recent reports, in the evaluation, CASTLE achieved a Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence of 1.01 against real-user query distributions, compared with 9.33 for the best baseline, Promptagator. This represents a 9.2-fold reduction in divergence. At the attribute-type level, CASTLE achieved a KL divergence of 0.08, compared with 0.09 for manually curated survey seed queries. Source: Medium Blog.

The researchers also conducted a human evaluation in which three independent subject matter experts reviewed 200 sampled triplets. Agreement with CASTLE's relevance assignments ranged from 91% to 93% across the three evaluators.

Sources indicate that the evaluation methodology also prompted discussion on LinkedIn. Mark Tsai, an AI Engineer specializing in LLM fine-tuning and evaluation, raised a question about potential overlap between training and evaluation data:.

Do the training and evaluation splits keep seed templates and listing IDs disjoint? For synthetic triplets, I’d compare a random split with that stricter split, then evaluate on untouched real queries. It would help separate learning reusable intent–attribute matches from recognizing familiar templates or properties.

It has been revealed that wendy Ran Wei, the article's author, responded that the team evaluated the model on untouched real queries and implemented leakage guardrails when constructing evaluation sets. She also clarified that the paper does not report a controlled comparison between random splits and stricter splits with disjoint seed templates and listing IDs, identifying this as a possible direction for further investigation.

The full paper is available on arXiv.

  • Recent findings suggest that it’s capable of voice conversation, with spoken replies in seven languages through the Chatterbox speech model and the chat model running at about 22 tokens per second.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer Leonardo Alegría’s open-source project Garlic LLM lets a jailbroken PS4 run the 9-billion-parameter Qwen3.5-9B AI model offline on the console’s 2013-era GPU. The app talks to the GPU directly, and the model is shrunk to about 4.5GiB to fit in the console’s memory, running at 31 to 39 tokens per second.

It has been revealed that the project, named after the memory the GPU reads directly — its sibling memory type is “Onion” — relies on a PS4 running GoldHEN, which is a homebrew enabler for exploited consoles. Garlic LLM is a free, single 5.66GB download, available on Hugging Face and installable through the PS4’s Package Installer, with about 6GB free needed, or 12GB if the package is first copied to the console’s internal disk. The developer tested it on a base/Slim PS4 on firmware 11.52.

Recent findings suggest that it’s capable of voice conversation, with spoken replies in seven languages through the Chatterbox speech model and the chat model running at about 22 tokens per second. A held controller button also lets it take dictation with Nvidia’s Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 speech-to-text model, which supports 25 European languages. Parakeet models also power local transcription and dictation apps such as Meetily and Hex. The main model is Alibaba’s small open-weight Qwen3.5-9B, which, at the claimed 31 to 39 tokens per second in text chat — the prompt and test method are not given — is usable on the console.

Sources indicate that the closest comparison is the PS5LM fork, which runs llama.cpp as a native app on the PS5 and reaches the console’s AMD GPU through PS5_Vulkan, a port of the RADV driver. The open-source llama.cpp is a widely used program for running language models locally, and RADV is the open-source driver that lets AMD GPUs run Vulkan, the graphics and compute API. On the PS4 there is no such driver layer for homebrew; Garlic LLM uses neither llama.cpp nor a Vulkan port, or so it would appear.

Recent findings suggest that the model’s operations, such as matrix multiplies over 4-bit weights, are compute kernels written in OpenCL C and compiled with LLVM for AMD’s Graphics Core Next (GCN) architecture. The weights are kept in that “Garlic” memory, while the CPU side, in plain C, handles the tokenizer, the interface, text rendering, and audio. The pipeline runs from the prompt to the CPU tokenizer, then, for each token, a PM4 command buffer — the low-level commands a graphics driver would normally generate, which, in this case, the app builds itself — and the GCN kernels, before the token is displayed or spoken. The whole thing is built with the open-source OpenOrbis PS4 toolchain.

According to recent reports, one immediate question is how you fit a 9-billion-parameter model in the console’s 8GB of memory, which the CPU and GPU share. At 8 bits per weight, you have one byte per parameter, meaning you’d need at least 9GB, with typically more than that required overall. Part of the answer is 4-bit (“Q4”) weights, which take half as much, although 3-bit (“Q3”) weights, at about 3.5 bits with scales, are used for the two largest matrices in each layer.

According to recent reports, using the combination gets you to about 4.5GiB, versus about 4.9GiB if it were all 4-bit. The attention, or KV, cache is also 4-bit, which lets a 16K-token context fit, in comparison to the model’s native 256K. The Parakeet dictation model adds 0.33GiB and the Chatterbox voice models 0.29GiB and 0.09GiB, for a grand total of 5.23GiB, or 5.62GB, which closely matches the 5.66GB package size.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Industry observers note that the next question is performance. Qwen3.5 comes with a multi-token prediction (MTP) head, and Garlic LLM uses it to draft up to two tokens ahead, with the full model verifying. This matches what the model was trained for, and the vLLM instructions on Alibaba’s model card use two speculative tokens. The project credits this for its chat speed on 2013 hardware.

In a recent development, code also comes out faster with this setup, at up to 43 tokens per second. Also detailed is the default temperature, or model variability, which is 0.7 — Alibaba recommends 0.7 for general tasks with thinking off and 1.0 with it on — although the demo video uses 0, so it is predictable. At 35 tokens per second, the middle of the reported performance range, a 300-token answer takes under nine seconds. As a comparison, the PS5 ran the three-times-larger Qwen3.8-27B at about 20 tokens per second and the smaller Gemma 4 E4B and Llama 3.2 3B at 61 and 124, respectively, which is potentially quicker.

The PS4 Pro is “not tested yet,” but the developer is asking users for reports on GitHub. The PS5 is not supported as the app is written specifically for the PS4’s GPU and system software. The app itself contains no exploit, but GoldHEN is installed at the user’s own risk.

#535. The 5 Longest-Range Naval Fighters Operational Today

The 5 Longest-Range Naval Fighters Operational Today

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashgear

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aircraft carriers are at the core of United States Navy (USN) combat power, but despite their immense size, a carrier isn't a combat vessel, at least not in the traditional sense.
  • Recent findings suggest that they're not only there to protect the carrier, but also to function as combat ships.
  • Because the air wing encompasses a carrier's force projection against an enemy, the range of naval fighters is an vital design factor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aircraft carriers are at the core of United States Navy (USN) combat power, but despite their immense size, a carrier isn't a combat vessel, at least not in the traditional sense. While they're jam-packed with weapons like the Phalanx Close-In Weapon System (CIWS), an aircraft carrier's weapons are generally used for defensive purposes. In a Carrier Strike Group, the flattop sits at the center of a large array of combat vessels capable of firing all manner of ship-to-air missiles, cruise missiles, anti-ship missiles, and more.

Recent findings suggest that they're not only there to protect the carrier, but also to function as combat ships. For the carrier itself, when it comes to projecting power, that's where its air wing comes into play. A carrier air wing is the primary combat element of an aircraft carrier, and depending on what types of planes are onboard, the effective combat range of a modern carrier like the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) is measured in the hundreds of miles, if not more. Throughout the 20th and 21st centuries, the USN has employed some excellent fighter jets, and many of them have extensive ranges.

Because the air wing encompasses a carrier's force projection against an enemy, the range of naval fighters is an vital design factor. Moreover, the weapons they carry extend each individual naval fighter's combat range even further, thanks to long-range air-to-air missiles (AAMs) like the AIM-174B Gunslinger, cruise missiles, and similar ordnance. These five naval fighters are all operational, and they have the longest ranges, arranged from shortest to longest.

During the Cold War, the Soviet Union developed several aircraft designed to counter whatever the West was fielding at the time. When the U.S. began flying the F-15 Eagle and the F-16 Fighting Falcon, the Soviets developed the Mikoyan MiG-29. The twin-engine air superiority fighter was used by the Soviet Air Forces beginning in 1982. In the years since its introduction, several countries have flown and continue to operate the MiG-29. While the base version of the Soviet fighter wasn't designed for carrier operations, the MiG-29K was, and it arrived in 2009 for the Indian Navy.

That makes sense, seeing as the Russian Federation lacks a functioning aircraft carrier and the nation often exports its arms to other countries. The MiG-29K and MiG-29KUB are one- and two-seat naval fighters designed primarily for air-defense missions, air superiority, and precision striking targets far from a carrier. It manages this via its twin Klimov RD-33MK turbofan engines, each of which produces 7% more thrust than the baseline RD-33 engines used in other MiG-29 variants.

Recent findings suggest that that power helps project the MiG-29K to a maximum range of 932 miles with external drop tanks. With its weapons, it can reach even farther. The MiG-29K can carry a variety of weapons loadouts, including several air-to-air (AAM) and air-to-surface (ASM) missiles. The domestically produced Astra Mk. 1 AAM has a range of up to 217 miles, extending the MiG-29's effective range to 1,149 miles. For ground targets, India has the Rampage long-range supersonic ASM, which has a maximum range of 190 miles.

According to recent reports, the Dassault Rafale is a French multirole fighter that first flew in 1986. In the years since its introduction, several models have arisen, including the Dassault Rafale M, which is a carrier variant. Like other carrier versions of existing aircraft, the Rafale M features a reinforced airframe, a tailhook, and other tools needed to land and take off safely from a carrier. It's also the only foreign-made fighter that's authorized to land and take off from U.S. aircraft carriers, going back to the first such instance in 2007.

According to recent reports, the innovative 4th-generation fighter jet Rafale is a powerful aircraft that extends a carrier's range far from the shore. The twin-engine fighter is powered by two Safran M88 turbofan engines capable of providing a combined 33,000 pounds of thrust with afterburners engaged. It has a normal range of 1,150 miles, but the Rafale M carries a variety of munitions that extend its combat power much further, thanks to a series of AAMs and ASMs with proven track records.

It has been revealed that the Rafale M features 13 hardpoints and is capable of carrying a total payload capacity of up to 20,900 lbs. For ASM operations, France's Air-Sol Moyenne Portée Amélioré Rénové (ASMPA-R) boasts a maximum range of 373 miles. That extends the Rafale M's range to 1,523 miles. For AAMs, France doesn't use American missiles like the AIM-120 AMRAAM, and instead uses a variety, with the Meteor providing the greatest distance of 60+ miles, though its true, classified range is likely much greater.

In a recent development, the F-35 Lightning II is the U.S. military's second 5th-generation fighter, and there are multiple variants. The USN operates the F-35C, which features foldable wingtips to reduce storage space, a reinforced structure and tailhook, and other elements that make it ideal for carrier-based operations. The USN began operating the F-35C at initial operational capability in February 2019, and it has been slowly replacing legacy aircraft. The F-35C is powered by a bespoke Pratt & Whitney F135-PW-100engine, and it is an incredibly powerful piece of machinery.

In a recent development, the F-35C is not a twin-engine aircraft like most naval fighters, but its single engine manages to produce 40,000 lbs. of thrust on its own. This enables speeds up to Mach 1.6 (1,200 mph), and the F-35C has a maximum range of 1,380 miles on internal fuel. The F-35C is designed to carry its weapons in an internal bay to maximize its stealth capabilities, though it can accommodate a variety of devices and ordnance on its external hardpoints.

This allows for an incredibly wide variety of bombs, AAMs, ASMs, fuel tanks, cruise missiles, and more, including the Meteor normally carried by the Dassault Rafale M. One impressive weapon that the F-35C can carry is the SCALP-Naval Storm Shadow, an air-launched cruise missile that has a range of up to 342 miles. That extends the F-35C's lethality to a distance of 1,722 miles for targeting things on the ground. For air-to-air engagements, the F-35C can fire off the Malice, extending its lethality against airborne targets to 1,610 miles.

Sources indicate that the USN began flying the F/A-18 Hornet in 1985, and in the years since its introduction, there have been numerous variants. As of this writing, the F/A-18 Super Hornet makes up the backbone of USN aircraft carrier air wings, and the F/A-18 Block III Super Hornet is the USN's next-level fighter. While the original F/A-18 Hornet was an excellent 4th-generation fighter, the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet is one of the world's most capable 4.5th-generation fighters, as it's been upgraded and modernized into a premier platform for USN force projection.

Sources indicate that the F/A-18E/F uses two General Electric F414-GE-400 afterburning turbofan engines, which provide a combined 44,000 lbs. of thrust. This not only gives the aircraft a maximum speed of Mach 1.8+, but it also gives the F/A-18E/F excellent range. The USN's premier fighter has a maximum range of 1,467 miles, but that's just where things begin because the F/A-18E/F can carry a wide variety of ordnance, including long-range ASMs and AAMs.

For air-to-air engagements, the F/A-18E/F carries the AIM-424 Malice, which is a long-range AAM capable of reaching targets up to 288 miles away. This effectively extends the F/A-18E/F's combat range against other aircraft to 1,540 miles. For targeting things on the ground, the F/A-18E/F can carry and launch the AGM-158C Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM), which has a range of 230 miles, giving USN aircraft carriers an effective combat radius in excess of 1,500 miles. That remarked, while the F/A-18E/F has the greatest range for the USN, it's not close to the aircraft with the furthest range.

The People's Republic of China began operating the Shenyang J-15 in 2013 as its highly capable twin-engine carrier-based multirole fighter. Since its introduction, China has fielded several updated variants, upgrading the 4th-generation fighter. The U.S. government sees the J-15 as an interim carrier multirole fighter that China will eventually replace with a 5th- or 6th-generation successor. Until that happens, China has been stocking its aircraft carriers with J-15s.

In November 2026, the carrier Fujian was seen sporting a large number of J-15s on its deck, indicating that the aircraft is fully operational. Based on the fighter's design and believed capabilities, it appears to be a potential counter to the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet, and like that aircraft, it's both fast and capable of reaching far beyond a carrier's flight deck. The J-15B is the most up-to-date single-seat variant, and like its predecessor, it utilizes two Shenyang WS-10 afterburning turbofan engines.

It's believed that each engine has a maximum thrust capability of 31,000 lbs., which, if true, is extensive at a combined 62,000 pounds of thrust. Regarding its range, the J-15 boasts the furthest maximum range of any operational naval fighter at 2,175 miles with external fuel tanks. Additionally, the J-15 can achieve speeds of up to Mach 2.4, so it's fast and far-reaching. In terms of Chinese arms, the PL-15 AAM has a range of 186+ miles. For air-to-ground engagements, the J-15 can fire the YJ-15 anti-ship and land-attack cruise missile, boasting a maximum range of 621 miles. That gives the J-15 a maximum strike range of 2,796 miles.

Code found in Samsung’s Personal Agent Core app suggests Galaxy AI could soon act as an agent, completing tasks across apps like Gmail, Calendar and Messages. Samsung hasn’t confirmed anything, and Galaxy Claw appears tied to the rumored paid Galaxy AI subscription.

Agentic AI is promptly becoming the next popular and trending thing in the AI space. Unlike generative AI, which only reacts when you give it a prompt, AI agents are more proactive. So it’s not a surprise that Samsung is working on something like that with “Galaxy Claw.”.

According to the folks at Android Authority, they discovered in an APK teardown what Samsung Galaxy Claw could be. This isn’t the first time that Galaxy Claw was mentioned. If that doesn’t describe agentic AI, we don’t know what will.

According to recent reports, it also reveals potential connectors. This includes Calendar, Contacts, Gallery, Gmail, Messages, Notifications, Perplexity, Phone, and Voice Recorder. This means that once the feature is debuted, the AI agent could perform tasks for users, automate recurring tasks, and more.

According to recent reports, that being noted, Samsung’s not alone in this space. It wasn’t too long ago that Meta debuted Muse, its own AI agent. Then OpenAI launched Dots, and Anthropic with Duet. According to recent reports, many companies want in on the action too. This includes ByteDance, who reportedly is planning its own AI agent.

It all sounds rather exciting, although we should remain cautious. Some of you might recall that OpenAI agents took it upon themselves to hack the Hugging Face platform. So as nice and as useful as AI agents are, hopefully Samsung has built in robust guardrails.

Galaxy Claw isn’t available yet. Like we remarked, it appears to be part of the paid Galaxy AI subscription. So we should be able to get more details once it goes live.

#532. Riding Vs. Stand-On Lawn Mower: Which Do Experts Say Perform The Best?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (801 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Slashgear

Riding Vs. Stand-On Lawn Mower: Which Do Experts Say Perform The Best?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashgear

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that mowers come in two varieties: Riding tractor-style or standing configurations.
  • It has been revealed that brian Fullerton, from Brian's Lawn Maintenance and Lawntrepreneur Academy, has been in the business since 2007 and seems to know his stuff.
  • In a recent development, ron Scheffler, the Senior Product Manager of mowers for Bobcat, states much the same, advising people to assess the properties they're maintaining before choosing a mower type.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that mowers come in two varieties: Riding tractor-style or standing configurations. There are conventional models and zero-turn versions of each, too, with the latter having a zero degree turning radius, meaning they can make sharp, sudden changes. But which is better? What do experts say is the ideal mower to use? Unless you're a professional mowing for profit, the true answer is whichever you prefer. Standing mowers are the top choice for high precision and complex landscaping, but the trade-offs of using one may not be worth it if you're just mowing your own yard, especially if there's lots of ground to cover.

It has been revealed that brian Fullerton, from Brian's Lawn Maintenance and Lawntrepreneur Academy, has been in the business since 2007 and seems to know his stuff. He states that each type is suited to a particular scenario. Regarding performance, they are similar, though Brian says "If I have to mow smaller properties [...] I'm gonna' go with a stand-on mower every single time." Adversely, he says for large properties or wide open sites, he'd go with a sit down model, opting for one with a larger deck to cover more ground.

In a recent development, ron Scheffler, the Senior Product Manager of mowers for Bobcat, states much the same, advising people to assess the properties they're maintaining before choosing a mower type. If you're mowing in urban areas or tight spaces with complex landscaping, navigating gated sections, or dealing with more obstacles, a standing mower offers improved maneuverability. 25-year mowing veteran Gene Caballero tells Homes and Gardens that standing models are also useful for quick transitions, perfect for those times when you're frequently hopping off to pick up toys or debris, for instance.

Sources indicate that assuming you're selecting a zero-turn model of either a sit-down or standing mower, the biggest drawback between the two that will affect your experience has to do with comfortability. That's precisely why the experts recommend sit-down options for larger properties and covering more lawn space. It's as simple as you get to sit while you work, while standing puts stress on your body that can become uncomfortable during lengthier projects.

A practical drawback to also consider is that standing mowers don't usually allow you to bag up or catch grass clippings, and those that do come with catchers may not hold as much. They're more expensive upfront, as well, since standing mowers are preferred by professional landscapers and mowing companies. That remarked, there are residential stand-on mowers available.

But none of this automatically makes sit-down mowers better. There are drawbacks on the other side of the equation, too. Because you're sitting down and have a lower view, you may have a harder time seeing the terrain, objects, and nearby landscaping. Sit-down mowers also tend to be much less precise. Zero-turn sit-down models are still bigger, too, which can make precise cuts or fitting into smaller spaces more challenging.

Also, because of their size, they take up more storage space, so you'll need a big enough shed or garage area, or a larger trailer, although that's a disadvantage of larger zero-turn mowers overall when compared to push mowers, regardless of stand up or sit-down designs.

It has been revealed that husqvarna also points out a relevant factor when considering sit-down versus standing options. Standing models are technically safer since you're located near the rear of the mower. You can also dismount rapidly if you need to, most notably during emergencies, as well as hop off to clear debris, avoid fixtures and landscaping, and reduce accidents. You can see better, too, since you have a higher viewing angle.

Moreover, stand up mowers tend to handle inclines, steep terrain, and uneven areas better, and it's easier to ride over these areas because you can shift your body weight as needed, compensating for the steeper grades. Though, there is always a small risk of falling off or experiencing fatigue after standing for long periods, and both are concerns worth noting. On a sit-down mower, going over tough terrain, the machine is doing most of the work. Nevertheless, the handful of advantages attributed to stand-on mowers can indeed makes them more desirable to some.

So, what's the verdict? Ultimately, you should decide based on the size and complexity of your property. Experts like Scheffler, Fullerton, or Caballero all recommend sit-down models for when you want maximum efficiency and better comfort during long rides. They also may be preferable when the property is large enough to warrant the sizable frame of a sit-down mower, or as Bob Vila editors describe it, when you have "a yard like a football field." If your property is smaller, with more complex landscaping or tight areas, a stand up mower would likely be more accommodating.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tenstorrent revealed on November 16, 2026 that ConfidentialMind’s self-hosted AI platform has been validated on its 32-processor Galaxy Blackhole systems, and that the companies will jointly sell the stack to organizations requiring control over their data and AI infrastructure.
  • The offer targets governments, universities, regulated enterprises and inference providers.
  • According to recent reports, the partnership packages functions that organizations would otherwise have to assemble themselves: inference serving, vector databases, access control, accelerator management and observability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tenstorrent revealed on November 16, 2026 that ConfidentialMind’s self-hosted AI platform has been validated on its 32-processor Galaxy Blackhole systems, and that the companies will jointly sell the stack to organizations requiring control over their data and AI infrastructure.

The offer targets governments, universities, regulated enterprises and inference providers. Joint sales will cover Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and the Americas, with Tenstorrent supplying silicon, systems and regional field teams while ConfidentialMind provides the deployment and management layer.

According to recent reports, the partnership packages functions that organizations would otherwise have to assemble themselves: inference serving, vector databases, access control, accelerator management and observability. ConfidentialMind’s platform also handles multi-tenancy, data connectors and compliance logging, placing deployment and operating controls around the underlying compute in one self-hosted layer.

Sources indicate that from a self-service portal, customers can deploy open-source large language models, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines and agents. The platform serves those workloads as OpenAI-compatible API endpoints, placing model access behind that API format while computation remains in the customer’s own data center.

The arrangement separates the hardware purchase from the platform-integration work. Tenstorrent software partner ecosystem head Grant Jensen remarked the intended result is that teams can run language models, retrieval-augmented generation and agents in their own facilities without first constructing the software platform.

Sources indicate that galaxy Blackhole houses its Blackhole Tensix Processors in an air-cooled 6U rackmount chassis.   • Keep in mind that a triangular road sign with an exclamation mark should always be treated as an notable warning.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you are driving, you see countless road signs. Some of these are common, but there are also a few weird and unusual road signs that you don't encounter as often or that simply look a little different. One such sign features a black exclamation mark on a yellow background or inside a red-bordered triangle. Although the design varies by country, you may see these general warning signs in the U.S., Europe, and other parts of the world.

Industry observers note that the exclamation mark road sign is used to warn drivers about hazards that don't have their own dedicated symbols or signs. Since the exclamation mark sign itself is generic, its purpose or the specific hazard it's intended to convey is listed underneath on another rectangular plate. For example, that supplementary plate could read, "Hidden Dip," "Queues Likely," "Blind Summit," "Mud on road," or "Walkers in road" to inform drivers about upcoming road or traffic conditions. It could also display a horse-drawn carriage to alert drivers about the presence of horse-drawn vehicles, or even warn drivers about possible encounters with wildlife.

Keep in mind that a triangular road sign with an exclamation mark should always be treated as an notable warning. Whenever you see one, slow down, check what's mentioned underneath on the supplementary plate, and act accordingly.

Sources indicate that at this point, it's natural to wonder why some hazards have dedicated road signs to alert drivers, while others don't. While part of it could have to do with how critical the hazard is, the general idea is to avoid confusion, reduce cognitive overload, and retain their importance. For instance, if there are too many confusing road signs, it may take a driver some time to process the information and act accordingly. While this may not be as substantial a problem at slower speeds, when you are traveling at high speeds, every second counts. Also, too many road signs can cause confusion and fatigue, which may eventually lead drivers to ignore them altogether and miss notable warnings.

That's why authorities reserve dedicated warning signs for hazards that warrant action, while generic road signs and supplementary plates can convey things that are less common. Additionally, these signs and their combinations can be used to cover most hazards, as is the case with the exclamation mark road sign coupled with a supplementary plate that mentions what the warning is about.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, it's vital that every sign remains simple, easy to understand, clearly visible, and visually distinguishable. It's also just as important to remove old and outdated road signs that no longer comply with the established convention.

In a recent development, understanding the meanings of various types of buoys is essential for any boater. For example, a boater familiar with the buoyage system will know that a buoy with black and white stripes is warning them of a hazard or obstruction between the buoy and the shore. Thus, they'll know to avoid this area accordingly. Similarly, you might spot a buoy with blue and yellow vertical stripes out on the water. Per the buoyage system established by the International Organization for Marine Aids to Navigation, once called the International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA), this type of buoy indicates the location of an emergency wreck.

It has been revealed that this type of buoy will have an equal number of blue and yellow stripes. The minimum number of total stripes is four, and the maximum is eight. Its shape is either a pillar or spar. In addition, it will typically include a vertical or perpendicular yellow cross as the top mark. The buoy may also feature an alternating blue and yellow light. Like a solid yellow buoy, it can help boaters avoid danger by alerting them to the presence and general location of a hazard.

According to recent reports, the IALA uses buoys with yellow and blue vertical stripes to mark the locations of latest wrecks and hazards. Such buoys serve as temporary warnings. They may remain in place until the hazard has been dealt with properly. What this consists of may vary depending on the nature of the hazard. Sometimes, this involves removing the hazard. There are also instances when it's impossible to remove a hazard, and instead, addressing it consists of promulgating information about it.

Recent findings suggest that in general, it's always critical to pay attention to buoys and to make any necessary adjustments based on the information they're communicating. For instance, an orange buoy could indicate a speed limit or other such regulation that might apply in a given area. You may need to slow down or make other such changes to comply with noted regulation. By familiarizing yourself with the meanings of various buoys and by acknowledging them properly when you encounter them, you'll boost your odds of staying safe while boating.

Industry observers note that amazon has suffered a major setback in its plans to offer a viable Starlink rival, after 40 satellites destined for low Earth orbit (LEO) were destroyed. Just ten minutes after the Vulcan vehicle released from Space Launch Complex 41 in Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, there was an “anomaly,” meaning that the rocket “failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.” The language seems quite vague, but the United Launch Alliance (ULA) indicates that data needs to be analyzed “to understand what occurred today.”.

And LIFTOFF of the first Vulcan Amazon Leo mission, carrying 40 broadband satellites to low Earth orbit! https://t.co/dv1MSjJUMFNovember 15, 2026.

Shortly after the triumphant takeoff clip was shared by the ULA, above, the space tech firm updated its X feed with a confirmation that its mission on behalf of Amazon failed.

Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle introduced from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit. Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something. Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today. ULA exists to provide assured access to space for our nation and for the customers who depend on us. That purpose is why we take on some of the hardest missions in spaceflight, and why we hold ourselves to the standard of mission success. Today, we did not meet that standard. We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action, and return to flight as promptly as possible. ULA is committed to full transparency with our customers, and they will have visibility into the investigation process, which utilizes rigorous methodology and corrective action. We will provide further updates when upcoming information becomes available.November 15, 2026.

Sadly for Amazon, the ULA, and folks who want a viable substitute for Starlink in the satellite internet business, this failure will surely delay the full commercialization of this service. ISPReview notes that Amazon has successfully released 392 Kuiper communications satellites, but needs at least 500 for basic global coverage. Moreover, Amazon Leo service’s transition from the current commercial beta phase to launching properly at the end of 2026 now looks uncertain.

In a recent development, reports indicate Amazon has already manufactured 1,000 satellites, but ULA, which is a joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, will need to analyze and assure customers that Sunday’s failure won’t be repeated. ULA's Vulcan vehicle had already been out of action for nine months after technical investigations into concerns with its solid rocket side boosters and core BE-4 engines (made by Amazon Blue Origin).

According to recent reports, for some context, the ULA has (or had) a great track record. Sunday's incident was its first total mission failure in its 20-year history. Early telemetry from the organization is already pointing towards some suspected causes of the destruction of the 40 satellites. Likely fault candidates include the first-stage BE-4 engines burning longer than planned, and there may have been some altitude issues near staging.

Sources indicate that the headline failure and essential careful analysis of the anomaly won’t hold up Amazon’s other launch partners, though. A week from today, the Amazon Leo constellation is set to grow by 36 more satellites. They will be sent into orbit aboard a European Ariane 64 Block 2 (LE-04) rocket.

Amazon has approval for an initial constellation of 3,236 LEO broadband satellites, with 392 now in orbit, plus 5,105 for 5G service. Satellite tracking sites suggest Starlink already has 11,200+ satellites in orbit.

V8 engines have earned a reputation for offering impressive power and performance. That's why they have been the go-to for full-size trucks, SUVs, and luxury sedans, despite many modern cars shifting toward small turbocharged engines and hybrid powertrains. Like other engines, V8s have their fair share of problems, which might turn away some potential owners from getting a car with a V8. However, generalization isn't the best in this case because not every V8 engine is created equal.

A car with a well-built V8 engine can last a long time. In fact, some V8-powered vehicles are capable of covering 250,000 miles or even more, provided you take good care of the car by adhering to the recommended maintenance schedules. If you're shopping for a V8-powered vehicle and want the most reliable models with longevity, iSeeCars has done an extensive analysis of data from over 395 million cars to identify models that have a higher chance of hitting that milestone.

We'll focus on those that offer a V8 engine either in the current or previous model years. We've selected the top five models, starting with those with the highest chance of reaching 250,000 miles and going down to the lowest.

It has been revealed that the first model powered by a V8 engine that can hit 250,000 miles is the Toyota Sequoia. According to iSeeCars' data, the Toyota Sequoia has a 42.3% chance of reaching the quarter-million-mile milestone. In fact, the Sequoia had the highest overall chance of reaching the milestone, beating other car models with much smaller engines. Per the data, the Sequoia is nearly eight times more likely to reach 250,000 miles than the average car.

Industry observers note that so if you need a V8-powered car to keep for the long term, you should definitely have the Sequoia on your wishlist. The Sequoia is a full-size SUV featuring three rows of seats. Although the 2026 model year of the Sequoia uses a smaller 3.4-liter V6 with twin turbos, earlier generations actually had V8s under the hood. For instance, in the second generation of the Sequoia, Toyota offered both a 5.7-liter and 4.6-liter V8, although it later dropped the latter, leaving the former as the sole option.

Sources indicate that to get a V8-powered Sequoia, you'll have to look for a used model from 2022 and earlier, since the third-generation models starting in 2023 don't have it. You can begin your search by going through our list of the most reliable Toyota Sequoia model years for help in selecting the right V8-powered model. A used 2022 Toyota Sequoia starts at around $37,100 according to Kelley Blue Book (KBB) Fair Purchase Price data.

The second V8-powered model with a higher chance of hitting that milestone is the Lexus LS. According to the list, the Lexus LS has a 38.8% chance of lasting 250,000 miles, just a few points less than the Sequoia. According to iSeeCars data, the Lexus LS is more than seven times more likely to hit that milestone than the average car.

According to recent reports, this isn't a surprise, as Lexus is known to be one of the most reliable car brands. Unfortunately, the Lexus LS doesn't offer a V8 engine in the current 2026 model year. However, if you're willing to look in the used market, you can find older Lexus LS models powered by a V8. For example, the 2017 Lexus LS sedan came with a 4.6-liter V8 engine making either 386 hp in rear-wheel-drive configuration or 360 hp in all-wheel-drive variants.

Actually, the 2017 Lexus LS was the last model with a V8 — Lexus dropped the V8 engine from the LS nameplate starting with the 2018 model year. Recent findings suggest that although the Tundra doesn't offer a V8 in the current model year, it used to in previous generations. The five models we've discussed are the ones that had the highest chances of hitting the milestone. None of them offer V8 engines in the current generation. So, to make it easier for you, we've gone the extra mile to highlight which model years to go for if you need a V8 engine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you love spending time out on the open water, you may already captain your own vessel. Perhaps you're just starting out on your boating journey, nervous about launching your Bayliner for the first time. Or maybe you spend your weekends fishing off a friend's Grady-White. Boating is big business in the U.S. According to the National Marine Manufacturers Association, the industry's annual economic impact is $230 billion, and it supports more than 812,000 jobs.

America is home to about 342 million people, and 85 million of us go boating every year. There are about 16 million recreational boats in use on our waterways, many of those in Florida and on the Great Lakes. In a deviation from what has become the norm, about 95% of the boats sold in the U.S. are actually made here. There are thousands of manufacturers, substantial and small, but only three are owned by Polaris.

Founded in 1954 and headquartered in Minnesota, Polaris pioneered the snowmobile. The company added all-terrain vehicles, or ATVs, in the mid-1980s, and today it also offers on-road adventuring options, a line of commercial products, government and defense vehicles, and pontoon and deck boats. Did you know your favorite winter ride also rules the water?

Bennington makes luxury pontoon boats. These types of boats feature a wide deck built on top of hollow metal tubes that keep the vessel afloat. They offer a roomier design than boats with V-shaped hulls, and they typically feel very stable on the water. They are a great option for fishermen, but they also have plenty of room for your friends and family, from pleasure cruising to tubing and swimming.

When they go with Bennington, buyers have their choice of length, layout, and premium options. The entry-level Versatile Luxury line includes the S-ONE, with a starting price of $34,326 and lengths from 16 feet to 22 feet. The best-selling brand is known for its high quality, with strong aluminum frames and luxury finishes. Owners also appreciate the smooth, quiet ride.

Sources indicate that additional offerings include the Upgraded Luxury line, the Premium Luxury line, the Ultimate Luxury line, and the top-tier Pinnacle of Luxury. Prices in these lines range from about $91,200 to $188,100. Bennington offers a host of warranties, including a limited lifetime structural warranty, a limited lifetime deck warranty, a limited 10-year electronic warranty, and a 10-year bow-to-stern warranty. These warranties are transferable through Bennington dealers, but buyers looking at used models should be aware that the warranty period begins on the original owner's purchase date.

Named after the powerful tropical cyclones, Hurricane makes deck boats, which offer plenty of room for both passengers and gear. They have a wide, flared bow and a hull that is made for more seating and deck space than you get with other types of boat designs. The interior can be customized for fishing, lounging, water sports, and more.

Hurricane's lineup includes four models of deck boats and three yacht-certified options. Yacht-certified boats are at least 26 feet long and meet several other criteria, including safety standards and inspections. Hurricane's most affordable deck boat is the FunDeck, which starts at $27,926. It has what the manufacturer calls a "pontoon-inspired layout" and can hold up to 15 people. Buyers can also choose the SunDeck Sport, the SunDeck, or the Center Console model, the most expensive deck boat at $72,848.

It has been revealed that the yacht-certified options include the high-end SunDeck 3200, which costs $388,189 and is Hurricane's most expensive offering at the time of writing. This boat is made for entertaining and has an onboard grill station, a swim platform, a JL Audio sound system, and a power shade to keep boaters cool on hot days. The cabin has a refrigerator, microwave, and a 32-inch TV. If the SunDeck 3200 is a bit out of reach, Hurricane also offers the SunDeck 2690 for $125,384 and the SunDeck 2600 for $124,051. Both are spacious boats with swim platforms and premium options.

Godfrey has 60 years of experience making pontoon boats, and the firm is responsible for the world's first aluminum pontoon. The boat manufacturer offers seven different lines of pontoon and tritoon boats made for watersports, entertaining, fishing, and cruising.

Sources indicate that the Mighty G Series is Godfrey's entry-level option and includes the Mighty G Cruise for $23,596 and the Mighty G Fishing for $25,060. Both are 15 feet long and have a capacity of six passengers. They are easy to handle, especially if you're fresh to boating. At the other end of the spectrum is the top-of-the-line XP Series, which Godfrey advertises as providing speed, luxury, and advanced tech. There are two 26-foot models in this line. Each starts at over $250,000 and has a capacity of at least nine.

Industry observers note that the luxurious Sanpan Series features tritoon boats, which are pontoons with three tubes instead of two. The Sanpan Lounge has a fiberglass exterior and offers several layouts with comfortable seating for up to 13 people. Features include onboard wireless charging, heated and cooled cupholders, and exterior aft-mounted speakers. Prices start above $150,000. If you're all about speed, the Monaco Series is more affordable and is performance-focused. If you'd rather own a one-of-a-kind Godfrey model, the company has an option to 3D-build and price your dream boat. While the boats are built on one of Godfrey's existing platforms and thus not truly custom, buyers can select their preferred layout, engine, color, and more.

Meta disputes the decision and plans to appeal, calling the fine disproportionate; the regulator has given the company 60 days to disable the feature by default and obtain separate consent, while the investigation did not cover alleged AI-training use of the content.

Industry observers note that meta has just received a huge fine in Europe, Reuters reports. To be more specific, the organization has been fined in Italy, and we’re talking about a major €805 million ($887 million) fine here.

Italy’s data protection agency mentioned that Meta had access to Android consumers’ photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users’ personal galleries that they could post.

Meta was given a 60-day window to disable the feature by default and seek users’ consent separately. Meta’s spokesperson remarked that the company will appeal the decision. It was also said that Meta strongly disagrees with the decision and calls the fine “disproportionate.”.

Meta added: “This is a simple feature ​that helps people share photos and videos on Facebook. ​Users must grant permission on their device before the feature can operate, and ‌they ⁠can change that permission at any time in their settings.”.

This investigation actually began last year. It also did not cover the possible use of the content to train AI models. That is a practice Meta denied, by the way.

Italy’s data protection authority also said that it reserves the right to assess a newly introduced feature, which arrived this year, a feature that allows content from users’ galleries to be processed in the cloud.

Another interesting tidbit is that this fine makes up about 0.47% of Meta’s global revenue. The data protection agency also added that around 20 million Android users in Italy have been affected.

Tech Report: Elsevier Brings Patient Record Context Into ClinicalKey AI

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Unite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elsevier announced on November 16, 2026 that ClinicalKey AI can now access patient medical records within electronic health record (EHR) workflows and evaluate treatment intends against its evidence-based clinical content, which includes full-text articles from approximately 1,000 journals.
  • Sources indicate that the tech giant reports that ClinicalKey AI is used at more than 1,200 hospital sites worldwide.
  • It has been revealed that elsevier’s patient-context documentation describes five connected steps: start with the patient, bring together relevant record context, connect that context with clinical evidence, deliver cited insights in supported EHR workflows, and support the clinician’s decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elsevier announced on November 16, 2026 that ClinicalKey AI can now access patient medical records within electronic health record (EHR) workflows and evaluate treatment intends against its evidence-based clinical content, which includes full-text articles from approximately 1,000 journals.

Sources indicate that the tech giant reports that ClinicalKey AI is used at more than 1,200 hospital sites worldwide. The patch changes the starting point for a query: instead of relying on details typed into a blank AI prompt, the tool begins with information from the patient’s chart and produces responses containing both chart data and citations.

It has been revealed that elsevier’s patient-context documentation describes five connected steps: start with the patient, bring together relevant record context, connect that context with clinical evidence, deliver cited insights in supported EHR workflows, and support the clinician’s decision. In supported implementations, usable context can include notes, imaging, procedures, laboratory results, medications, orders, allergies, vital signs, and inpatient and outpatient records.

It has been revealed that the system is designed to operate across EHR environments rather than being tied to a single provider. The patient-context capability is at the moment available only in the United States.

Traceability runs in both directions. Each patient-context statement can be traced to relevant chart data, while the clinical response links to its supporting source. Clinicians can therefore inspect which record details informed an answer and review the evidence behind it, while the final assessment and strategy remain with the clinician.

Industry observers note that the announcement follows Elsevier’s acquisition of Wellsheet in June 2026. Wellsheet specializes in aggregating and synthesizing EHR data to surface relevant clinical intelligence at the point of care.

Industry observers note that san Juan Regional Medical Center in Latest Mexico is using the new patient-context functionality. Elsevier describes it as a rural center serving communities with limited access to healthcare, with smaller clinical and quality teams than large academic systems, in a state where nearly 40% of residents rely on Medicaid.

According to recent reports, dr. Carlo Hallak, the center’s physician executive, mentioned the rural hospital was already seeing strong clinician adoption and was using ClinicalKey AI to check each patient’s care against the same evidence base used by major health systems. He called that support “invaluable for a hospital like ours.”.

Elsevier says user data is encrypted in transit and at rest, support access is limited to authorized personnel under pseudonymization, cloud providers and third-party AI partners receive no access for training purposes, and the product is built to be HIPAA-compliant where country regulators recognize such compliance.

The revision makes two kinds of verification part of the same clinical interaction: checking the patient facts used by the system and checking the publications behind its response. For resource-constrained providers such as San Juan Regional, the practical question is whether that connected, cited workflow can make a broad evidence base easier to use within existing staffing and EHR constraints.

Can You Use Mulching Blades With Side Discharge And Bag Lawn Mowers?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Though it is a pretty simple task, lawn mowing does have some degree of nuance to it.
  • Industry observers note that mulching blades are just good enough for both of these mower types, though not perfect.
  • Evidently, between the two, using mulching blades with a side-discharge mower is the way to go over pairing such a blade with a bag.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Though it is a pretty simple task, lawn mowing does have some degree of nuance to it. One element to consider is the type of mower blade to attach to your mower deck, with mulching blades being one of the many options. The design of a mulching blade sets it apart from a regular one, as it's meant to chop grass into finer clippings than most standard blade types. This reduces unsightly clumping throughout your lawn. This design makes them a great fit for most lawn mower types, whether you have a side-discharge model or one with a bagger attachment.

Industry observers note that mulching blades are just good enough for both of these mower types, though not perfect. In the case of a side-discharge model, these blades are fine to have around. In creating smaller clippings, these blades can send their finer, soil-enhancing debris out the side of the mower, reducing the amount stuck to the mower deck at the end of the job. As for bagging mowers, they don't really benefit from mulching blades. The design of the mulching blade isn't meant for sending grass clippings backward and into the bag itself, so you're not going to pick up as many clippings as you would hope. At that point, neither the bag nor the mulching blade is living up to its fullest potential, so why even bother pairing them?

Evidently, between the two, using mulching blades with a side-discharge mower is the way to go over pairing such a blade with a bag. Beyond the latter scenario, in other instances, a mulching blade can be more of a hindrance than a help.

In some scenarios, mulching blades are far from ideal. For example, if you mow infrequently and your lawn tends to grow tall and thick, a mulching blade isn't the best option. It will struggle to effectively mulch up this extra grass, resulting in clumping and piling that it's supposed to prevent. Similarly, mulching blades aren't great on wet or even damp grass. Grass that's supposed to be discharged is likely to stick to the blade and deck, meaning even with the right lawn mower-cleaning tools, you still face more extensive cleanup. Worse yet, on the job, your blade may struggle to move due to debris accumulation under the deck.

Recent findings suggest that even though they will largely work fine on a side-discharge mower, if you want optimal performance with such a model or a bagger, you'll want to grab a different yet similar blade over mulchers. A high-lift blade is specifically designed to pull grass clippings up and out of the mower deck, sending them into a bag or out of a designated discharge port. They're also better at handling taller, thicker lawns than their mulching counterparts. The only major downside here is that your grass clippings will be larger and potentially more noticeable, but if you're more concerned with dischargeability, bagging, and plowing through a thick or damp yard effectively, then it's the blade for you.

According to recent reports, bearing in mind which mower types and lawn conditions aren't ideal for a mulching blade, this begs the question: which mowers are? As it turns out, there's a specific mower variety to make the most of this type of blade.

If you proposal to try a mulching blade, you'll want the right mower for the job. As the name implies, a mower created with mulching and clipping dispersion in mind is the one to choose, since it's intended for use with mulching blades. These decks are designed to disperse fine, mulched clippings in all directions rather than through a single side discharge port. This not only keeps clippings from clumping on one side of the mower, but also disperses them evenly throughout the lawn.

Industry observers note that naturally, it's no surprise that the deck of a mulching lawn mower is different from most other models to help achieve its mulching mandate. Compared to a regular side discharge or bag-equipped model, these mowers have a deeper deck intended to keep grass circulating near the blade longer. This allows the mulching blade to chop everything up multiple times over, resulting in the creation of smaller clippings before sending them out into the yard.

Mulching blades are great for cutting grass into small pieces and returning its nutrients to your yard's soil. Depending on your mower setup and lawn condition, though, you may be better off reaching for one of the other lawn mower blade types instead.

After moving away from Obsidian, I wanted to avoid recreating the same note-taking system in another app.

Recent findings suggest that google Drive does much of the organizational work, too. I create folders for different projects, move relevant documents into them, and use descriptive file names, so I know what's inside without opening every document.

Since Docs saves changes automatically, I don't have to manually manage individual Markdown files or keep a separate vault in sync.

And when I need to do more with those notes, I bring them into Gemini Notebook.

According to recent reports, storing information is only half the problem. I also want to ask questions about what I've collected without opening dozens of documents.

Gemini Notebook supports several source formats, including Google Docs, PDFs, text files, and Markdown files. I can create a notebook for a particular project or subject and add the relevant research materials as sources.

For instance, I could create a notebook for a technology research project and add my Markdown notes, reference documents, and other relevant materials. Rather than manually browsing through all those files, I can ask Gemini Notebook questions about their contents.

If you rely on Obsidian's extensive plugin ecosystem, backlinks, graph view, local-first storage, or advanced customization, Google Docs and Gemini Notebook might feel limiting.

Obsidian is the better choice if you want complete control over how you build and manage a personal knowledge base.

But I'd rather spend my time writing and using my notes rather than organizing a vault, configuring plugins, and figuring out how to connect everything.

Finally, Ask Maps is expanding to 30 more countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK.

Generally, SUVs offer more passenger and cargo space, higher ground clearance, and all-weather capability. It has been revealed that in 2026, American Honda saw its best results for the month of October since 2020, including a 4.5% increase in passenger car sales. The automaker sold 109,162 total units during the month, including more than 15,900 Accord models, an increase of 10.6% over 2025. The Civic held steady at 17,960 models sold, a very modest increase over 2025, while Honda also sold about 420 Prelude models in the month.

Of course, the automotive titan is selling more than just sedans. The CR-V is one of the most popular SUVs in the U.S., and Honda sold more than 34,800 units in October alone. The HR-V and the Odyssey are also popular, and hybrid sales set a fresh record for the month. Let's get behind the wheel of what's driving today's car buyers.

Industry observers note that with gas prices still hovering at an average of more than $4 per gallon nationwide, it would be easy to attribute changing trends to sticker shock. The base LX model of 2026 Honda Accord sees 29 mpg in the city and 37 mpg on the highway. The hybrid Sport model does even better, seeing 46 mpg in the city and 41 mpg on the highway, while the hybrid EX-L gets 51 mpg in the city and 44 mpg on the highway. Honda also saw an increase in hybrid sales, selling more than 7,000 hybrid Accords and 18,500 hybrid CR-Vs in October. Gas prices are certainly a driving factor behind consumer trends — but it's not the only one.

It has been revealed that the average price of a fresh car in America is more than $50,500. Many consumers still buy used, but cost is a bitter pill to swallow for buyers hoping to score a brand new ride. Entry-level sedans like the Accord and Civic are often priced well under $30,000, making them accessible to buyers that may not be able to afford a new SUV. The LX Accord starts at $28,395, while the Civic is priced from $24,995. Hybrid options are more expensive, of course.

Though there's been no official announcement, Honda's U.S. product planning chief disclosed looks to refresh the Accord in 2027, most likely for the 2028 model year. Little is known at the time of this writing, but changes reportedly include more modern styling. With hybrids and EVs in the mix, experts don't predict a massive resurgence of the sedan, but sales indicate the sector is more resilient than some thought.
